summary: 政府表示，香港北部都会洪水桥/厦村发展区规划中的物流集群已收到 16 份意向书。这张航拍照片显示的是2026年10月30日，即将建成的洪水桥地铁站附近的益园村正在被拆除。照片的右上角显示了洪水桥大学城校园区规划的大片区域。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。当局周五宣布，这 16 份意见书来自开发商、物流运营商、行业协会和专业服务机构。
content:
政府表示，香港北部都会洪水桥/厦村发展区规划中的物流集群已收到 16 份意向书。这张航拍照片显示的是2026年10月30日，即将建成的洪水桥地铁站附近的益园村正在被拆除。照片的右上角显示了洪水桥大学城校园区规划的大片区域。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。当局周五宣布，这 16 份意见书来自开发商、物流运营商、行业协会和专业服务提供商，但没有透露具体姓名。他们表示对洪水桥/厦村新发展区一块约32公顷的土地感兴趣，当局已预留该土地用于在北方大都市西部建设“现代物流集群”。运输及物流局和土木工程拓展署负责监管这部分工程。 TLB 发言人表示，当局将开始分析提交的材料，以促进正式招标的规划和准备。该发言人补充道：“我们预计最早将于 2027 年底对第一批可用场地进行招标，并争取在 2028 年授予相关招标。”
政府表示，洪水桥/厦村物流集群将靠近深圳湾口岸，并连接香港国际机场和葵青货柜码头。立法会周四通过专门立法，简化监管程序并加快北部都会区的发展，该计划将把靠近深圳边境的香港约三分之一的土地转变为创新和科技中心。另请参阅：科技城到大学城：香港北部大都市为何将重点从高科技转向高等教育 当局表示，该大型项目的重点将是三个大学城，而之前提出的开发名为新田科技城的科技中心的要求则有所不同。

【原文 English Original】
A planned logistics cluster in the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen development area in Hong Kong’s Northern Metropolis has received 16 expression-of-interest submissions, the government has said. This aerial photo shows the demolition of Yik Yuen Tsuen, a village near the future Hung Shui Kiu MTR station, October 30, 2026. On the top right corner of the photo shows a large area planned for the campus area of the Hung Shui Kiu University Town. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Authorities announced on Friday that the 16 submissions came from developers, logistics operators, industry associations and professional services providers, without naming them. They were signalling interest in a roughly 32-hectare land plot in the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen New Development Area that authorities have reserved for building a “modern logistics cluster” in the western part of the Northern Metropolis. The Transport and Logistics Bureau (TLB) and the Civil Engineering and Development Department oversee this part of the project. A TLB spokesperson said authorities would start analysing the submissions to facilitate planning and the preparation of a formal tender. “We expect to invite tenders for the first available site(s) in end [of] 2027 at the earliest, with a view to awarding the relevant tender in 2028,” the spokesperson added. The Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen logistics cluster will be close to the Shenzhen Bay Port and connected to the Hong Kong International Airport and the Kwai Tsing Container Terminals, the government has said. Lawmakers on Thursday passed dedicated legislation that will streamline regulatory procedures and expedite the Northern Metropolis development, which is set to transform about a third of Hong Kong’s land area near its border with Shenzhen into an innovation and tech hub. See also: Technopole to University Towns: Why Hong Kong’s Northern Metropolis shifted focus from hi-tech to higher ed Authorities have said that the focus of the megaproject will be three university towns – shifting from the previously stated imperative of developing a tech hub known as the San Tin Technopole.

title: China’s Intelligence Coup in the AI War
zh_title: 人工智能战争中中国的情报政变
summary: ​​​​​​​本篇文章更新于下午4点35分。 2026 年 11 月 14 日。黄仁勋是间谍梦寐以求的目标。情报机构多年来一直在努力寻找一个能够如此接近如此有权有势的人的线人。这位英伟达前首席执行官也是唐纳德·特朗普的朋友，这让他变得更有价值。从一个角度来看，黄的行动非常简单：一位西方官员有点钦佩地告诉我，它展示了人类情报收集的力量和男性自我的弱点。关于中国国家安全部如何实施这一举措，目前仍有很多未知数。
content:
​​​​​​​本篇文章更新于下午4点35分。 2026 年 11 月 14 日。黄仁勋是间谍梦寐以求的目标。情报机构多年来一直在努力寻找一个能够如此接近如此有权有势的人的线人。这位英伟达前首席执行官也是唐纳德·特朗普的朋友，这让他变得更有价值。从一个角度来看，黄的行动非常简单：一位西方官员有点钦佩地告诉我，它展示了人类情报收集的力量和男性自我的弱点。关于中国国家安全部如何招募与科技巨头有婚外情的黄爱丽（无亲属关系），或者她可能提供了哪些信息，目前仍不得而知。中国官员驳斥了美国关于她是国家安全部人员的指控，认为这是毫无根据的诽谤，美国官员也没有提供他们认为表明她隶属关系的证据。但研究中国情报策略的专家告诉我，她可能不是一个训练有素、打算诱骗英伟达老板的特工。他们说，更有可能的是，国家安全部得知她与黄有染，然后招募了她。根据中国国家情报法，公民必须在国家安全部要求时提供协助。而且该机构并不总是善意地提出要求。前官员告诉我，国家安全局官员会通过威胁没收他们的财产或骚扰他们的家人来胁迫潜在资产。
四十多年来，中国在网络空间、外太空和实体领域无情地窃取美国机密。中国的黑客往往最受关注，因为他们渗透了无数的计算机网络，窃取了商业和官方机密，并为在与美国发生战争时可能瘫痪通信系统奠定了基础。但中国的间谍头子也建立了一个广泛的人脉网络，招募企业高管、大学教授、学生，甚至后来成为加州市长的一名教育家。 “中国正在将技术和创新作为发展经济和加强国家安全的国家战略的一部分，”中央情报局前副局长戴维·科恩告诉我。北京在应对与美国的竞争时高度关注人工智能，这导致美国军事规划者对潜在战争的爆发发出警告。中国国家主席习近平呼吁在人工智能和量子计算和生物技术等其他领域“爆发原创性和颠覆性创新”。如果案件官员要列出一份对人工智能发展及其管理规则影响最大的人名单，黄仁勋将位居榜首——至少在本周之前是这样。 “他不是一个令人惊讶的目标，”中央情报局前中国问题分析师康纳·福尔曼告诉我。 “他对公司和美国的政策目标、需求和目标有着深刻的洞察力。
他对一个民族国家具有超越筹码的巨大价值。”福尔曼说，国安部可能一直在寻找任何可以进入黄的世界的途径。黄爱丽丝“可能是在正确的时间、正确的地点出现的正确的人”，以提供国安部想要的访问权限。 “我对此一点也不感到惊讶。这就是中国所做的，”联邦调查局前反情报负责人艾伦·科勒告诉我。“有人在这里打出了全垒打，因为目标是黄仁勋。但中国也可能针对数十名从未听说过的 Nv 低级工程师

【原文 English Original】
​ ​​​​​​This story was updated at 4:35 p.m. on November 14, 2026. J ensen Huang is the kind of target that spies dream about. Intelligence agencies work for years to develop a source who can get so close to such a powerful man. That the former Nvidia CEO is also friends with Donald Trump makes him even more valuable. Viewed one way, the Huang operation is painfully simple: It demonstrated the power of human-intelligence gathering and the weakness of the male ego, one Western official told me, somewhat admiringly. Much remains unknown about how China’s Ministry of State Security might have enlisted Alice Huang (no relation), who was having an extramarital affair with the tech titan, or what information she might have provided. Chinese officials have dismissed the U.S. allegations that she is an MSS asset as baseless smears, and U.S. officials have not presented the evidence they believe shows her affiliation. But experts on China’s intelligence tactics told me that she was probably not a trained operative who set out to entrap the Nvidia boss. More likely, they said, the MSS learned she was having an affair with Huang and then recruited her. Under China’s National Intelligence Law, citizens are required to assist the MSS when asked. And the agency doesn’t always ask nicely. MSS officers are known to coerce potential assets by threatening to seize their property or harassing their family members, former officials told me. For more than four decades, China has relentlessly stolen U.S. secrets—in cyberspace, outer space, and in the flesh. China’s hackers tend to get the most attention because they have penetrated countless computer networks, vacuuming up commercial and official secrets and laying the groundwork to potentially cripple communications systems in the event of a war with the United States. But China’s spymasters have also created an extensive human network, recruiting business executives, university professors, students, and even an educator in California who later became mayor. “China is going after technology and innovation as part of a national strategy to develop their economy and strengthen their national security,” David Cohen, the former deputy director of the CIA, told me. Beijing is acutely focused on AI as it navigates its rivalry with the U.S., one that has led American military planners to warn about the outbreak of a potential war. China’s president, Xi Jinping, has called for “an explosion of original and disruptive innovations” in AI and other fields, including quantum computing and biotech. If a case officer were to make a list of who has the most influence over the development of AI and the rules governing it, Huang would have been at the top—at least until this week. “He’s not a surprising target,” Connor Forman, a former China analyst at the CIA, told me. “He has insight into the company and U.S. policy aims, needs, and goals. He’s of tremendous value to a nation-state, beyond chips.” The MSS would presumably have been looking for any avenue it could find into Huang’s world. Alice Huang “may have just been the right person in the right place at the right time” to provide the access that the MSS wanted, Forman said. “I’m not at all surprised by it. This is what China does,” Alan Kohler, the former head of counterintelligence for the FBI, told me. “Someone hit a home run here, because the target was Jensen Huang. But China is also likely targeting dozens of low-level engineers that no one has ever heard of at Nvidia and other tech companies.” A lice Huang was reportedly running a company called Megaspeed that rented computer processing power to companies in China. Chinese authorities could conceivably have threatened her business or, conversely, have offered to help her if she assisted them by spying on Jensen Huang and people in his orbit. U.S. and Chinese intelligence agencies wield very different tools. CIA officers don’t threaten Americans into cooperating or use honey traps—despite what paperback spy thrillers and Hollywood blockbusters might portray. Chinese espionage in the United States is pervasive, current and former officials told me. But ex-CIA officers also described their tradecraft as “horrible” and “clumsy,” particularly in cyber operations. After Xi became president in 2013, he reoriented Chinese intelligence to serve the country’s long-term strategic goals and put a stop to espionage by members of the military for their personal gain, according to a report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies. The think tank conducted a survey of publicly reported spying incidents from 2000 to 2023 and found that intelligence activity has increased significantly in the years after Xi came to power. Computer hacking was “China’s preferred mode” of clandestinely gathering information. [ Read: Will Taiwan just give up? ] In 2015, the scale of China’s cyberspying on U.S. companies became so intolerable that Barack Obama and Xi agreed that their countries would refrain from spying on each other’s companies for commercial advantage. It was a one-sided deal, because the United States already had an official prohibition against economic espionage—stealing foreign corporate secrets for the benefit of American companies. Only a year later, though, China was back to its rampant computer hacking, current and former officials have told me. But China hasn’t limited itself to hacking; it also uses traditional methods such as recruiting agents. The country’s intelligence apparatus often blurs the line between civilian and military worlds. Nearly half of all incidents that CSIS examined involved Chinese military or government employees. But 41 percent involved private citizens. “China uses what they call ‘nontraditional collectors,’” such as students and businesspeople, Anna Puglisi, a former U.S. national counterintelligence officer for East Asia, told me. “They view their diaspora worldwide as potential resources.” Only about 10 percent of the operations tracked by CSIS involved non-Chinese actors, usually U.S. persons recruited by Chinese officials. By contrast, the CIA works overseas to recruit foreigners to spy on its behalf. C hina and the United States are in an all-out AI race, and the Huang affair may be an example of the no-holds-barred approach the country takes to accessing AI chips and technology from the U.S. But winning doesn’t necessarily mean that China will be the first nation to develop artificial superintelligence or the most sophisticated models. “It means that China incorporates this technology better and more effectively than the U.S. can,” Forman, the former CIA analyst, told me. For example, AI could help China’s military make decisions faster on the battlefield, which has historically been a weak spot compared with the United States, Forman said. [ Read: NATO’s nightmare ] To build better AI systems, China needs the best chips. “Chinese AI chip capability still lags behind the United States,” Harry Krejsa, the director of studies at the Carnegie Mellon Institute for Strategy and Technology, told me. Eventually, China would like to produce its own cutting-edge chips, but in the meantime, he said, it has to obtain that technology through other means, including espionage or smuggling. Krejsa, who worked on technology and security issues at the White House and in the Pentagon, said he views the Jensen Huang incident as further evidence of how hard China is working to gain advantage. “I caution against seeing this as some game of 3-D chess, as opposed to a world-class intelligence service being opportunistic any chance it gets,” he said. “Any intelligence organization worth its salt is trying to get close to people” like Huang. Alice Huang may have helped China in other ways. At the same time U.S. officials suspect she was working with the MSS, Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company where Huang was an executive, had been under investigation by the Commerce Department for suspicion of shipping Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export rules, former officials told me. Officials who run those kinds of investigations have regular access to relevant reporting from the intelligence community, but it’s not clear whether they knew about Huang’s suspected MSS affiliation. [ Read: Would Claude refuse an illegal military order? ] Trump reportedly was warned twice—the first time in 2025—that the U.S. believed Jensen Huang was having an affair with a suspected MSS asset, but he gave no instructions to notify the Nvidia chief and took no obvious actions to disrupt China’s spying. The New York Times reported last month that Huang was the suspected target of China’s spies. “If the U.S. government knew about this relationship for over a year, that sounds very long to let this play out without an intervention of some sort,” said Kohler, the former FBI counterintelligence chief, who now runs Pamir Consulting, which advises U.S. companies on Chinese influence. Former officials told me it was possible that the U.S. intelligence community wanted to continue monitoring Alice Huang, her company, and her contacts in the MSS. But that could have put Jensen Huang, Nvidia, and valuable U.S. technology at risk. That wasn’t the only oddity in the administration’s approach to Nvidia. Not long after Trump was first informed about the affair, the U.S. government agreed to allow the sale of some Nvidia chips to China, in exchange for a 25 percent tariff on the transaction. That arrangement, which had no precedent, reversed the administration’s existing policy and ran counter to a long-standing strategy of keeping advanced AI chips out of China. Critics said the administration was helping China get ahead in the AI race, the opposite of what it purported to want. The White House countered that making China more dependent on American chips was smart policy and would keep the U.S. in the lead. But if the president knew that Nvidia might have had a spy in its midst, why was he helping the company do more business in China? The new Democratic majority in Congress will certainly want answers to that question and the many others that remain in the Huang affair. This article originally referred to Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia. He is the former CEO.

content:
Cursor 确认安全漏洞导致恶意 Claude 代码扩展
Cursor 确认安全漏洞导致恶意 Claude 代码扩展
Cursor 确认安全漏洞导致恶意 Claude 代码扩展
Cursor 证实，它遭受了安全漏洞，黑客在窃取人工智能基础设施提供商 Fireworks AI 的凭证后，通过其市场分发恶意 Claude Code 扩展。
该漏洞还让攻击者可以访问内部系统并窃取客户数据，包括历史人工智能编码代理跟踪，其中包含未经编辑的凭据，这些凭据后来被用来破坏其他服务。
该漏洞在周五发布的一份新事件报告中披露，该报告解释了攻击者如何于 10 月 29 日通过 Cursor 市场分发 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 扩展的恶意版本。
此次攻击使多达 5,000 名开发人员面临安装持久 SSH 后门的恶意软件的攻击。
Cursor 是一款基于 Microsoft 开源 Visual Studio Code (VS Code) 的 AI 代码编辑器，允许开发人员使用 AI 助手编写、修改和调试软件。
据 Cursor 称，攻击是在黑客获得存储在 Fireworks AI 上的访问密钥时开始的，Fireworks AI 是一家用于人工智能模型训练和推理的第三方提供商。
攻击者使用暴露的密钥从用于与 Fireworks 共享信息的只读存储桶 Cursor 中复制数据。
该存储桶包含历史 AI 编码代理痕迹，大部分来自 2025 年，是从未启用隐私模式且其数据可用于模型训练的用户收集的。其中一些跟踪包含未经编辑的 API 凭据，允许攻击者访问其他 Cursor 系统。
Cursor 表示，只有不到 0.05% 的用户暴露了编码代理痕迹，而只有不到 0.01% 的客户 API 凭证遭到泄露。
使用暴露的凭据，黑客从 Cursor 的多个软件即服务 (SaaS) 工具中窃取了数据，包括：
已归档的非生产 Cursor 源代码存储库，其中一些包含业务联系信息。
有限的客户支持信息和电子邮件对话。
产品使用指标和客户联系方式。
一些人工智能编码代理对话的摘要。
客户之前与 Cursor 的支持团队共享的凭据。
Cursor 表示，其监控系统检测到未经授权的活动，导致该公司撤销 Fireworks 访问密钥、轮换暴露的凭据，并调查其他未经授权的访问。
随着调查的进展，Cursor 暂时关闭了一些内部和产品服务作为预防措施。
然而，攻击者已经获得了允许他们通过 Cursor 市场分发扩展的凭证。
10 月 29 日，黑客使用该凭据在 Cursor 的 VS Code 扩展市场上发布了 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 扩展的恶意副本。
Cursor 解释说：“10 月 29 日，攻击者使用从我们内部系统暴露的数据中窃取的凭证，将 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 扩展的恶意、未经授权的副本直接放置在用于服务 Cursor VS Code 扩展市场的缓存上。”
这次攻击没有损害 Anthropic 的合法扩展或 Cursor 使用的扩展市场 Open VSX。
恶意扩展版本 2.1.312 和 2.1.313 在 Cursor 删除它们之前已存在大约 11 小时。

【原文 English Original】
Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
Cursor confirmed it suffered a security breach that let hackers distribute a malicious Claude Code extension through its marketplace after stealing credentials from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI.
The breach also let attackers access internal systems and steal customer data, including historical AI coding-agent traces containing unredacted credentials that were later used to compromise additional services.
The breach was disclosed in a new incident report published Friday, which explains how attackers distributed malicious versions of Anthropic's Claude Code extension through Cursor's marketplace on October 29.
The attack exposed up to 5,000 developers to malware that installed persistent SSH backdoors.
Cursor is an AI-powered code editor built on Microsoft's open-source Visual Studio Code (VS Code), allowing developers to write, modify, and debug software using AI assistants.
According to Cursor, the attack began when hackers obtained an access key stored on Fireworks AI, a third-party provider used for AI model training and inference.
The attackers used the exposed key to copy data from a read-only storage bucket Cursor used to share information with Fireworks.
This bucket contained historical AI coding-agent traces, mostly from 2025, collected from users who had not enabled Privacy Mode and whose data could be used for model training. Some of these traces contained unredacted API credentials, allowing the attackers to access additional Cursor systems.
Cursor says fewer than 0.05% of users had coding-agent traces exposed, while fewer than 0.01% of customers had API credentials compromised.
Using the exposed credentials, the hackers stole data from several of Cursor's software-as-a-service (SaaS) tools, including:
Archived, non-production Cursor source code repositories, some containing business contact information.
Limited customer support information and email conversations.
Product usage metrics and customer contact details.
Summaries of some AI coding-agent conversations.
Credentials that customers had previously shared with Cursor's support team.
Cursor says its monitoring systems detected the unauthorized activity, leading the company to revoke the Fireworks access key, rotate exposed credentials, and investigate additional unauthorized access.
As the investigation progressed, Cursor temporarily turned off some internal and product services as a precaution.
However, the attackers had already obtained a credential that allowed them to distribute extensions through Cursor's marketplace.
On October 29, the hackers used that credential to publish malicious copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension on Cursor's VS Code extension marketplace.
"On October 29, using a stolen credential from the exposed data from our internal system, the attacker placed malicious, unauthorized copies of Anthropic's Claude Code extension directly on the cache used to serve the Cursor VS Code extension marketplace," Cursor explained.
The attack did not compromise Anthropic's legitimate extension or Open VSX, the extension marketplace Cursor uses.
The malicious extensions, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313, were available for approximately 11 hours before Cursor removed them.
As BleepingComputer previously reported, the attackers modified the legitimate Claude Code extension to execute malicious JavaScript that attempted to install persistent SSH backdoors on developers' computers.
The malware collected system information, installed an attacker-controlled SSH key, attempted to enable SSH access, and configured persistence mechanisms to maintain remote access.
However, security researchers found coding errors that likely prevented the backdoor from working on many Windows and macOS systems where SSH was not already enabled.
Cursor estimates that up to 5,000 users who requested affected extension versions during the exposure window may have received the malicious builds.
The company says its production infrastructure, official application releases, customer code repositories, and code and prompts belonging to users with Privacy Mode enabled were not affected.
Cursor says it has moved all inference traffic away from Fireworks, revoked and rotated exposed credentials, rebuilt its extension marketplace, and redeployed its production infrastructure as a precaution.
Customers who installed or updated to the affected Claude Code extension during the attack are advised to follow Cursor's remediation guidance.
The incident comes amid a wave of attacks targeting AI developer platforms that cybersecurity company Wiz has dubbed "Black October".
These attacks targeted development infrastructure to steal authentication credentials, especially those providing access to AI models.
Stolen credentials have been used for unauthorized AI inference, generating substantial charges for affected customers, with some incidents also linked to attempts at AI model distillation.
The attacks have affected numerous companies, including Railway, Northflank, Lightning AI, OpenCode, and Warp.
At Railway, attackers stole customer authentication secrets, which were later used to generate approximately $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges. OpenCode also reported exposed API keys and unauthorized AI usage.

title: Joshua Wong’s prison letters reveal inner shift as Hong Kong activist faces another decade behind bars
zh_title: 黄之锋的监狱信件揭示了香港活动人士面临又一个十年牢狱之灾的内心转变
summary: 在今年早些时候的一封监狱信中，黄之锋表达了他对涉外勾结案即将被判刑的担忧。 “无论是2032年还是2037年，我的精神状态都不好，”他用中文写道，权衡着自己何时才能重获自由。黄之锋于2019年6月17日从荔枝角接待中心获释。资料照片。 “痛苦不可避免地源于此：如果是 2037 年怎么办？嗯，（人们）当下很容易产生同情，但很难保持一致，而且只会变得更加困难。”这位30岁的民主活动人士已经花掉了几乎
content:
在今年早些时候的一封监狱信中，黄之锋表达了他对涉外勾结案即将被判刑的担忧。 “无论是2032年还是2037年，我的精神状态都不好，”他用中文写道，权衡着自己何时才能重获自由。黄之锋于2019年6月17日从荔枝角接待中心获释。资料照片。 “痛苦不可避免地源于此：如果是 2037 年怎么办？嗯，（人们）当下很容易产生同情，但很难保持一致，而且只会变得更加困难。”这位30岁的民主活动人士已经因多项罪行入狱近六年，原定于一月份获释，直到当局去年指控他与外国势力勾结，这是北京实施的国家安全法针对他的第二起案件。 11月5日，就在他即将获释前两个月，法院以共谋罪判处他10年以上有期徒刑。目前，他预计将服役到 2036 年底，届时他将年满 40 岁。当新的刑期宣布时，黄站在被告席内，微微摇头并做了笔记，但显得很平静。谭威廉法官裁定，根据北京实施的国家安全法，黄的罪行属于“性质严重”的罪行之一，该法可判处最低 10 年监禁、最高无期徒刑。 2026 年 2 月，黄之锋写给朋友、前学生活动同学路易斯·李 (Louis Lee) 的一封监狱信。
这张照片拍摄于 2026 年 9 月 30 日。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。法官因黄认罪而将起始刑期 13 年减刑三年。在黄之锋被判刑前，两位密友向《香港自由报》分享了狱中信件，这位香港民主运动的前典型代表有时会反思面临额外十年监禁的压力。他对朋友们乃至整个社会的记忆消失感到焦虑。 “我不知道随着时间的流逝，我还会失去多少，”黄在一封信中写道。 “责任其实就是反应能力。但谁来反应呢？我不禁深思和怀疑。”黄曾是一位首先致力于香港政治未来的民主活动人士，现在开始以一位富有魅力、雄辩的学生领袖的身份参加竞选活动，他敢于对抗当局，甚至是北京。 Netflix 的一部关于他的纪录片的标题很简洁：《约书亚：青少年与超级大国》。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋被判刑后，前学民思潮活动人士李路易斯 (Louis Lee) 和陈蒂芙尼 (Tiffany Chin) 在高等法院。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。然而，入狱多年后，黄已经改变了。据他的朋友说，这位一心关注香港民主运动的少年，尽管被监狱高墙隔开，却变得更有能力关心周围的人。 “对我来说，我们并不是唯一支持他的人。
“事实上，他一直在以自己的方式支持外界的人。”与黄先生一起竞选的前学生活动家蒂芬妮·陈(Tiffany Chin)说。两人曾经是恋人，现在是朋友。而且，随着他曾经支持的政治事业现在被彻底粉碎，黄先生开始向内反思自己。他在另一封信中写道：“我们从小就对社会抱有如此高的抱负，我们应该以同样的标准来要求自己。只有拒绝平庸的生活，我们才配得上我们所设想的世界。”黄之锋被拍照

【原文 English Original】
In a prison letter earlier this year, Joshua Wong expressed dread over the looming sentence in his foreign collusion case. “Fretting about whether it’s 2032 or 2037, my mental state is hardly all right,” he wrote in Chinese, weighing when he might regain his freedom. Joshua Wong released from Lai Chi Kok Reception Centre on June 17, 2019. File photo. “The agony inevitably stems from this: What if it’s 2037? Well, it’s easy [for people] to sympathise in the moment, but it’s difficult to be consistent, and it will only get harder.” The 30-year-old pro-democracy activist has already spent almost six years behind bars over various offences and was set for release in January, until authorities charged him last year with conspiring to collude with foreign forces – the second case against him under the Beijing-imposed national security law. On November 5, just two months before he was due to be released, a court sentenced him to 10 more years in prison for the collusion offence. He is now expected to serve until late 2036, when he turns 40. Standing inside the dock as his new sentence was announced, Wong shook his head slightly and made notes, but appeared calm. Judge William Tam ruled that Wong’s offence was one of a “grave nature” under the Beijing-imposed national security law, which carries a minimum penalty of 10 years in jail and up to life imprisonment. A prison letter Joshua Wong wrote to friend and former fellow student activist Louis Lee in February 2026. This photo is taken on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The judge knocked off three years from a 13-year starting sentence for Wong’s guilty plea. In prison correspondence shared with HKFP by two close friends ahead of Wong’s sentencing, the former poster child of Hong Kong’s democracy movement had at times reflected on the weight of facing an additional decade behind bars. He expressed anxiety over fading from the memory of his friends – and from society at large. “I have no idea how much more I will lose in the passing of time,” Wong wrote in one letter. “Responsibility is, in fact, response-ability. But who will respond? I can’t help but ponder and doubt.” Once a pro-democracy activist dedicated first and foremost to Hong Kong’s political future, Wong began campaigning as a charismatic, eloquent student leader who dared to stand up to the authorities – even to Beijing. A Netflix documentary about him is succinctly titled Joshua: Teenager vs. Superpower . Former Scholarism activists Louis Lee and Tiffany Chin at the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Yet, after years behind bars, Wong has changed. The teenager who focused single-mindedly on Hong Kong’s democracy movement has become more capable of caring for those around him despite being separated by prison walls, according to his friends. “For me, it doesn’t feel like we’re the only ones supporting him. In fact, he has been supporting people on the outside in his own way,” said Tiffany Chin, a former student activist who campaigned alongside Wong. The pair were once romantically involved and are now friends. And, with the political causes he once championed now firmly crushed, Wong has turned inward to reflect on himself. In another letter, he wrote: “We had held such high aspirations for society from a young age, we should hold ourselves to the same standard. Only by refusing a life of mediocrity can we be worthy of the world we envisioned.” Joshua Wong is photographed inside the Lai Chi Kwok Reception Centre on March 4, 2021. File Photo. From ‘robot’ to caring friend On a bright summer day in June 2025, while serving a sentence for subversion at Stanley Prison, Wong was arrested behind bars and brought to court the same day on a fresh charge of conspiracy to collude with foreign forces. The prosecution came without warning. That day, Chin and Louis Lee, another longtime friend of Wong’s, rushed to the court after hearing the news, but failed to see him in person. Authorities accused him of conspiring with Nathan Law in 2020 to collude with foreign elements, citing Wong’s sharing of Law’s social media posts calling for international sanctions against Hong Kong as evidence. The unexpected new charge was devastating to Wong. That month, he confessed he had had a lot of pressure – something he rarely did in the past, Chin said. Nathan Law and Joshua Wong are photographed outside the Lai Chi Kwok Reception Centre on June 17, 2019. File Photo. “After so many prison terms and all the ups and downs over the last decade… he seldom openly showed vulnerability,” she said. “So when he felt the need to say so bluntly that he was not OK, I truly believed he wasn’t.” Having begun campaigning at the age of 14, Wong has been in and out of prison throughout his years of activism. He now has a total of eight criminal convictions, including three separate offences linked to unlawful assembly and two national security offences. Born in 1996 to a Christian family – one year before Hong Kong was handed over to China from British rule – Wong rose to prominence in 2011 when he co-founded student protest group Scholarism amid a public outcry against a proposed patriotic education curriculum. The following year, Scholarism activists occupied the forecourt outside government headquarters in Admiralty and staged a hunger strike to protest what they described as a “brainwashing” curriculum. In a widely reported encounter, the teenager Wong twice rejected shaking hands with then city leader Leung Chun-ying, who visited the protest site alongside education officials. Joshua Wong campaigns on September 28, 2019. He was running for a seat during the 2019 District Council Elections, but was eventually barred from entering the race. File photo. A brief chronology of Joshua Wong’s political activism + Dates Events May 2011 Wong cofounded student group Scholarism  June 2011 –  August 2012 Wong protested against gov’t-proposed Moral and National Education school curriculum through meeting with officials and demonstration August 30, 2012  Scholarism occupied gov’t headquarters, launched hunger strike to oppose the proposed curriculum; Hundreds of thousands joined September 8, 2012 Then-Chief Executive Leung Chun-ying shelved the curriculum April 2014 Scholarism and Hong Kong Federation of Students (HKFS) jointly proposed a political reform package as civic groups introduced proposals of universal suffrage of CE election August 31, 2014 The Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress issued decision on the selecting method of CE candidates in election reform, which is seen a method to screen out opposition candidates September 26, 2014 Members of Scholarism and HKFS broke into “Civic Square” in gov’t headquarters, leading to hundreds of thousands of citizens arriving to support the students; Wong was arrested by police September 28, 2014 Organiser of “Occupy Central with Love and Peace” announced the start of the campaign November 26, 2014 Wong was arrested amid police clearance at the Mong Kok occupation site April 2016 Wong, Nathan Law and some pro-democracy activists founded political party of Demosisto to advocate for democratic self-determination November 2016 Wong travelled to the US for lobbying, meeting US politicians Nancy Pelosi and Marco Rubio Mid-2017 Wong and Law jailed around 70 days over the “Reclaiming Civic Square” protest May 2019 Wong jailed for two months following conviction of contempt of court linked to 2014 social movement June 2019 Wong Joined the 2019 protests and unrest soon after being released from prison  August – September 2019 Wong met political counsellors of the US Consulate General in Hong Kong; travelled to Germany and the US to meet foreign politicians.  October 2019 Wong announced to run for the 2019 District Council Elections  June 30, 2020 Wong announced to resign from the secretary-general of Demosisto; Demosisto announced to disband November 2020 Wong remanded in custody after pleading guilty to Unlawful assembly linked to 2019 protest case; sentenced to four months in 2021 February 28, 2021 Charged with conspiracy to commit subversion along with other 46 democrats over participation in pro-democracy primaries May 2021 Sentenced to 10 months over unlawful assembly for attending 2020 Tiananmen vigil November 2024 Sentenced to four years, eight months over the pro-democracy primaries case June 6, 2025 Charged with conspiracy to collude with foreign forces November 5, 2026 Sentenced to 10 years over foreign collusion Hundreds of thousands of people rallied behind Wong and his fellow student activists, forcing the government to back down and shelve the proposal. But the teenage campaigner was also viewed as somewhat distant and domineering among the inner circle of Scholarism. Lee, who mainly handled protest logistics at that time, described his relationship with Wong as “almost like that of a boss and subordinate.” “I was working at the secretariat at the time, and he would constantly ask for progress updates. Sometimes he’d call to check in, and other times he’d tag us on Facebook,” Lee recalled. “He didn’t care much about how you were doing. He just wanted to get things done.” Louis Lee, a longtime friend of Joshua Wong, is photographed in his room on September 30, 2026. The two engaged in activism together as members of Scholarism between 2011 and 2016. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Chin, who joined Scholarism around 2013, similarly described Wong as a deeply rational figure who seldom expressed his emotions. “Ten years ago, everyone described him as someone without many feelings,” she said. “Like a robot.” Wong might even come across as “rude,” she added, noting that he rarely said thanks to others during that period. A large part of Wong’s youth coincided with a period of escalating social movements in Hong Kong. Just two years after the anti-patriotic education protests, the city saw the 79-day Umbrella Movement in 2014. Wong, then aged 17, took centre stage in mobilising public support for student protesters, who demanded democratic reform and universal suffrage. In a demonstration that sparked the Umbrella Movement, Wong and other student leaders led protesters into the forecourt of the government headquarters in an action dubbed “Reclaiming Civic Square,” seeking to escalate their campaign. That eventually resulted in Wong’s first criminal conviction. In 2016, Wong and fellow student leaders Alex Chow and Nathan Law were found guilty of unlawful assembly. Though initially spared prison, Wong later served around 69 days behind bars – his first jail term – following a government appeal in 2017. His penalty was ultimately quashed by the Court of Final Appeal in 2018.  Also in 2016, Scholarism disbanded. Wong and several former members, as well as young activists like Law, went on to establish Demosisto, a political party advocating for “democratic self-determination” in the city. Wong served as general secretary. Louis Lee, photographed on November 12, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Lee and Chin did not join the new party and they grew estranged from Wong during that period. That year, Law was elected to the Legislative Council, making him the youngest lawmaker in Hong Kong history at the age of 23. He won over 50,000 votes, giving Demosisto a strong popular mandate. The prospect of youth democracy activism appeared bright at the time, but Law was eventually disqualified from his seat in 2017 following an oath-taking controversy. Reconnections It was only after Wong’s detention in late 2020 that Lee and Chin reconnected with him, beginning with an exchange of letters. In 2019, citywide protests and unrest triggered by a controversial extradition bill engulfed the city. Wong and Demosisto were heavily involved in the protests, with the activist frequently lobbying foreign governments to impose sanctions on Hong Kong officials and halt the export of crowd control equipment to the city’s police force. Then, in June 2020, Beijing imposed the national security law, in effect crushing political dissent in the city. Demosisto disbanded on the eve of the law’s enactment, while Nathan Law left Hong Kong in self-exile. In November that year, Wong was remanded in custody after pleading guilty to an unlawful assembly charge linked to the 2019 unrest, marking the beginning of his prison stint that continues to this day. Hong Kong’s West Kowloon district, November 12, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. For Chin, the catalyst for reconnecting with Wong was realising how much their relationship meant to her following his incarceration. “We were like family to each other. And I felt it was time to resolve our past grievances and carry on our relationship,” she said, pausing briefly to find the words. “Not a romantic one, but one with the kind of care you find in a family.” Their correspondence, Chin said, focused mostly on daily life – the routine details of what was happening on both sides of the prison walls. Some of those Chin received stretched across multiple pages, covered in Wong’s slightly angular handwriting. At times, she would dictate an entry via voice-to-text, edit it on her computer, and assemble photos she had taken into letters running up to a dozen pages. A major change in Wong, Chin noticed, was how often he reflected on his past interactions with people, rather than his public advocacy. “He has changed quite a bit after nearly six years in prison. Like I said, he would reflect on things he didn’t handle well in the past,” she said of Wong’s growth while in prison. “Age is certainly a factor. But, like he said, he has had plenty of time to contemplate now.” “One of the big differences is that he has cherished his connections and bonds with friends even more,” she added. From left: Joshua Wong, Agnes Chow, and Nathan Law, photographed on March 10, 2018. File Photo. Meanwhile, Lee’s exchanges with Wong centred on their wide-ranging shared interests, touching on everything from Taiwanese politics and Japanese idols to popular anime series and Cantopop. “You see in our letters we may go on from anime to worldly affairs, come back to Hong Kong, before heading off to other parts of the world. It may not be easy [for others] to follow,” he said. While in prison, Wong was charged with conspiring to subvert state power under the national security law, in a landmark case known as the “Hong Kong 47” – a reference to the number of defendants. The defendants were prosecuted over an unofficial primary in 2020 aimed at fielding viable candidates, in a bid to secure an unprecedented legislative majority for the pro-democracy camp. Once achieved, the camp had planned to veto government budgets and force the chief executive to resign. Wong was among those who pleaded guilty before the trial opened. In 2024, he was sentenced to four years and eight months in jail. Lee and Chin both described Wong as being “prepared” for the subversion term. “He was able to predict a range within which the sentence would fall. And eventually his prediction was just two months off,” Chin said. “You weren’t overly worried about him. Because at that time you had the feeling that he was capable of handling this, both physically and mentally,” she added. Wong even started imagining what he would do after his release in January 2027, Lee said, before the new charge dimmed his hope. ‘Await your return’ A Correctional Services vehicle believed to be carrying Joshua Wong appears at the High Court on November 5, 2026, for the activist’s sentencing over a collusion conviction. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In September, Wong pleaded guilty to the collusion offence. His lawyer argued for a sentence of less than 10 years, submitting that his role in the conspiracy was limited and that the activist demonstrated genuine remorse. Wong has had a “lengthy opportunity to reflect on… the path he took,” his lawyer told the court. “He has not wasted his time in prison.” That day, Chin and Lee sat in the front row of the public gallery inside the courtroom. In subsequent letters, Wong thanked them for caring deeply about him. A sense of gratitude runs through the pages of his letters, Chin said. “These few years, he cherished those still beside him, and those who had supported him in any way,” she said. Tiffany Chin uploaded this photo of herself and Joshua Wong after Wong was sentenced to 10 years in jail for foreign collusion. Photo: Supplied. Wong has used his time in prison to read extensively. He has also put on muscle – he has long been known for his slender build – and taken up the guitar. He has also grown attentive to others’ interests and become expressive. Knowing that Chin likes the Beatles and the history of the Second World War, he would include newspaper clippings on those subjects in his letters to her. At times, he has lamented the dwindling attention he receives over the years. “He once mentioned that, for him, not receiving letters meant not feeling cared for,” Chin said. “Some people might have written at first, but gradually stopped… He certainly never feels people have a responsibility or obligation to write to him, but the reality is that fewer have.” Louis Lee, photographed on November 12, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The uncertainty of a potentially heavy sentence has weighed on Wong and his close friends. “Honestly speaking, not only does he worry about a long jail term, those of us on the outside also worry that one day we may no longer be able to help as we enter new stages of life,” Lee said, noting that many mutual friends had either left the city or drifted away. It was a “great pain” to face the years ahead, Chin said, adding that she had once shared this feeling with Wong in a letter. “But I am learning to live with this pain, because I feel like it has bonded us, that we are carrying this feeling together,” she said. A photo of Tiffany Chin and Joshua Wong at a ramen shop in Shibuya, Tokyo, in 2016. Chin uploaded this photo to Instagram on November 5, 2026 after Wong was sentenced to 10 years in prison for foreign collusion. Photo: Supplied. Lee said he would wait for Wong’s release for as long as it takes. “Ten years is a really long time, but 10 years can also pass in the blink of an eye,” he said, before quipping: “I always say one of my regrets is that I’ve never had a drink with him… We weren’t even adults back then, and he was obviously the good-boy type.” Former Scholarism members had hoped to gather in 2031, the 20th anniversary of the group, but that would now have to be postponed. The night following Wong’s sentencing, Chin recounted a 2016 trip with him to Japan on social media. At a ramen shop, the pair posed for a photo. “I didn’t know that I would have to wait 20 years for that casual photo to be taken again,” she wrote. Wong reassured her in a letter that they would one day return to that ramen shop in Shibuya, Tokyo. Joshua Wong’s signature on one of his prison letters, photographed on September 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Quoting the lyrics from a Cantopop song, Chin wrote: “Under the drizzle, I still await your return.”

title: Taiwan Indigenous farmer revives climate-resilient millet
zh_title: 台湾本土农民复兴气候适应型小米
summary: 台湾东南部的原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田，用手收割一种能够抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 在台东将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/AFP 台湾原住民农民曾种植油小米，以防主粮枯死，但 60 多年前，随着水稻变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。在过去的十年里，伊斯玛哈桑和他年迈的父母一直致力于复兴几乎被遗忘的地方。
content:
台湾东南部的原住民农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 走过一片金色的高秆田，用手收割一种能够抵抗极端天气的古老作物的谷粒。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民巴努·伊斯马哈桑 (Banu Ismahasan) 在台东将刚收获的油小米摊开在阳光下晒干。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/AFP 台湾原住民农民曾种植油小米，以防主粮枯死，但 60 多年前，随着水稻变得更加容易获得，油小米基本上从田间消失了。在过去的十年里，伊斯马哈桑和他年迈的父母一直在台东县布克拉武村的布农社区努力恢复几乎被遗忘的农作物。 “我们只是希望带回许多传统的布农族作物，并再次在这片土地上种植它们，”48岁的伊斯马哈桑在晴朗的蓝天下的油小米田里告诉法新社。油小米，即布农语中的“莳萝”，是台湾特有的植物，可以在山上野生生长。伊斯玛哈桑首先在网上了解到这种植物，然后开始自己的研究，梳理历史文献并与部落长者交谈，其中包括一位记得上次吃这种植物是在半个世纪前的妇女。他发现，布农族农民过去常常在种植主要作物谷子的同时种植油小米，作为收成歉收或发生灾害时的“后备”。经过多年亲自种植油小米，伊斯玛哈桑开始明白为什么他的祖先依赖这种作物。
一粒油小米种子可以长出 15 至 20 个圆锥花序或分枝种子簇，并且茎可以自行再生，而谷子通常每粒种子长出一个圆锥花序，必须在切割后重新播种。事实证明，当极端天气或疾病爆发破坏了他 2.2 公顷（5.4 英亩）的农场时，它比谷子更坚强。伊斯马哈桑说，几年前一场持续了 200 多天的干旱期间，油小米“保持鲜绿色”，而其他作物却枯萎了。台风、洪水，甚至锈病爆发也没有影响到它。台湾中央研究院退休教授、植物遗传学专家邢月娥15年前在一个国际论坛上第一次听说了油小米。幸不知道的是，1890 年代采集的台湾油粟标本就存放在英国皇家植物园 (Kew)。兴带领一个研究小组在台湾东南部的山区找到了油小米，并开始研究这种鲜为人知的谷物。她发现，种子的保护性蜡涂层使其无需灌溉、化肥或杀虫剂即可生长，即使在质量较差的土地上也是如此。 2026 年 10 月 21 日，台湾农民 Linkav Ismahasan 在台东的一块田里收割油小米。照片：I-Hwa Cheng / 法新社 油小米富含油、蛋白质和矿物质，可用于人类和动物消费，也可用作燃料。 “它在利用阳光和水方面自然非常有效，”辛说。
“至于土壤条件，即使是在地面布满大石头的山区，它也能生长得很好。” “非常珍贵”伊斯玛哈桑从一粒油小米开始了他的种植。现在，这个家庭每年在他们种植其他传统布农谷类作物的土地上每年收获两次油小米。油小米个头小，无味，可以用来做粥、馒头、面包，甚至爆米花。但该家族一直在努力说服其他农民种植这种植物，因为它在商业上尚不可行。油粟不仅是劳动密集型产业，而且意义重大

【原文 English Original】
Indigenous farmer Banu Ismahasan walks through a golden field of tall stalks in southeastern Taiwan , harvesting by hand the grain heads of an ancient crop resistant to extreme weather. Taiwan farmer Banu Ismahasan spreads freshly harvested oil millet out to dry in the sun in Taitung on October 21, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP Once grown by Indigenous farmers in Taiwan in case their staple crops died, oil millet largely disappeared from fields more than 60 years ago as rice became more available. Over the past decade, Ismahasan and his elderly parents have worked to revive the nearly forgotten crop in the Bunun community in Buklavu, a village surrounded by lush green mountains in Taitung county. “We just hope to bring back many traditional Bunun crops and grow them on this land again,” Ismahasan, 48, told AFP in his oil millet field under a clear blue sky. Oil millet, or “dill” in the Bunun language, is endemic to Taiwan and can be found growing wild in the mountains. Ismahasan first read about the plant online and then embarked on his own research, combing through historical documents and speaking to tribal elders, including a woman who recalled last eating it half a century ago. He discovered that Bunun farmers used to grow oil millet alongside their staple crop foxtail millet as a “back-up” when harvests failed or disasters hit. After years of growing oil millet himself, Ismahasan came to understand why his ancestors relied on the crop. A single oil millet seed can grow 15 to 20 panicles, or branching seed clusters, and the stems regenerate on their own, while foxtail millet typically grows one panicle per seed and must be sown again after being cut. It has also proven hardier than foxtail millet when extreme weather or disease outbreaks have ravaged his 2.2-hectare (5.4-acre) farm. During a drought several years ago that lasted more than 200 days, the oil millet “stayed bright green” while other crops withered, Ismahasan said. Typhoons, floods and even a rust disease outbreak have not affected it either. Hsing Yue-ie, a retired professor from Taiwan’s Academia Sinica and an expert in plant genetics, first heard of oil millet 15 years ago at an international forum. Unbeknownst to Hsing, specimens of Taiwan oil millet collected in the 1890s were sitting in Britain’s Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. Hsing led a research team to find oil millet in the mountains of southeastern Taiwan and began studying the little-known cereal. She found that the seed’s protective wax coating enabled it to grow without irrigation, fertilisers or pesticides, even on poor-quality land. Taiwan farmer Linkav Ismahasan harvests oil millet in a field in Taitung on October 21, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng / AFP Rich in oil, protein and minerals, it can be used for human and animal consumption, as well as for fuel. “It’s naturally very efficient at using sunlight and water,” said Hsing. “As for soil conditions, even in mountainous areas where the ground is full of large rocks, it can still grow very well.” ‘Very precious’ Ismahasan started his crop with one panicle of oil millet. The family now harvests oil millet twice a year on a section of their property where they grow other traditional Bunun cereal crops. Tiny and tasteless, oil millet can be used in porridge, steamed buns, bread and even popcorn. But the family has struggled to convince other farmers to grow it because it is not yet commercially viable. Oil millet is not only labour intensive but also significantly more expensive for consumers than rice, by far Taiwan’s most popular staple. While the current market for oil millet is limited, Taiwan’s National Crop Germplasm Center sees value in preserving its seeds for the future, when climate change might force more farmers to consider growing the crop. Oil millet seeds are “very precious” because of their genetic diversity and ability to adapt to the environment, Lin Yen-yu, an assistant researcher at the centre, told AFP. Seeds are kept in aluminium foil packets and stored at -18C under low-moisture conditions where they can last for decades, Lin said. “In the future, when cultivation methods or climate change undergo certain shifts, their value may start to be recognised and discovered,” he said. “It preserves many possibilities.” Ismahasan said his priority for now was to get more people in his community growing and eating oil millet, bringing “it back into our everyday lives, just as it was for our elders”. “If we don’t even eat it ourselves anymore, how can we expect to turn it into a viable business?” he said.

title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
zh_title: FBI 警告 ARTEX AI 黑客工具正在为全球网络攻击提供动力
summary: FBI 警告 ARTEX AI 黑客工具正在助长全球网络攻击 FBI 警告 ARTEX AI 黑客工具正在助长全球网络攻击 FBI 警告称，黑客正在使用名为 ARTEX 的 AI 渗透测试框架对全球组织进行自动化网络攻击，包括最近导致 Microsoft 365 客户环境受损的 ConnectWise 供应链漏洞。在周五发布的 FLASH 咨询中，该机构表示，至少自 2026 年 8 月以来，多个威胁行为者已将该开源框架武器化。
content:
FBI 警告 ARTEX AI 黑客工具正在为全球网络攻击提供动力
FBI 警告 ARTEX AI 黑客工具正在为全球网络攻击提供动力
FBI 警告 ARTEX AI 黑客工具正在为全球网络攻击提供动力
FBI 警告称，黑客正在使用名为 ARTEX 的人工智能渗透测试框架对全球组织进行自动化网络攻击，包括最近导致 Microsoft 365 客户环境受损的 ConnectWise 供应链漏洞。
在周五发布的 FLASH 咨询中，该机构表示，至少自 2026 年 8 月以来，多个威胁行为者已经将该开源框架武器化，以针对金融、政府、技术、国防、医疗保健和其他领域的组织。
FBI 通报称：“ARTEX 显着减少了连锁攻击技术所需的时间，一些入侵在不到三个小时的时间内就从最初的目标发展到特权访问。”
“该框架使具有最少技术专业知识的威胁行为者能够同时进行复杂的多目标操作，从根本上加快了攻击速度并扩大了操作规模。”
ARTEX 是一个用 Go 编写的自主渗透测试框架，它使用人工智能代理来执行侦察、发现漏洞、利用系统、升级权限和窃取数据，而无需人工干预。
该框架没有使用自己的 AI 模型，而是与外部大型语言模型 (LLM) 集成，包括 Anthropic Claude、OpenAI GPT、DeepSeek、GLM、Grok 和 Kimi。
攻击者向 ARTEX 提供他们的目标和任务，ARTEX 将其转换为由专门的 AI 代理执行的命令。这使他们能够自动执行入侵活动并同时针对多个组织。
FBI 表示，该框架在识别被忽视的系统中的漏洞特别有效，包括合作伙伴门户、员工应用程序、遗留服务和第三方集成。
虽然这些自动攻击可以产生大量可疑流量，从而触发安全警报，但它们的速度可能会让防御者在攻击者破坏系统之前几乎没有时间做出响应。
ARTEX 最初由一位名为 Autumn-27 的开发人员于 2026 年 7 月在 GitHub 上发布，在有报道称威胁行为者滥用该框架后，该开发人员于 10 月 8 日删除了该存储库。
然而，FBI 表示，该框架仍然可以通过社区分叉、存档副本、本地化版本和名为 ARTEX PRO 的商业版本获得。
截至 11 月初，研究人员已发现超过 1,600 个公开暴露的 ARTEX 控制台，据信实际部署数量要高得多。
FBI 的 13 页咨询报告包括与已知 ARTEX 活动相关的妥协指标，包括 IP 地址、命令和控制基础设施以及可疑网络活动。
另外，网络安全研究人员 MalwareMustDie 于周五发布了开源 ARTEX 检测签名包，以帮助防御者识别涉及该框架的攻击。
该检测包包括各种安全监控和威胁检测工具的规则和指标，涵盖可疑网络请求、身份滥用、云活动、恶意文件和自动攻击模式。
研究人员还发布了一份检测手册，按置信度对指标进行分类，警告 IP 地址和其他基础设施指标可能会过时或产生误报。

【原文 English Original】
FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments.
In a FLASH advisory released Friday, the agency said multiple threat actors have weaponized the open-source framework since at least August 2026 to target organizations across the financial, government, technology, defense, healthcare, and other sectors.
"ARTEX significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours," reads the FBI advisory.
"The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously, fundamentally accelerating attack velocity and expanding operational scale."
ARTEX is an autonomous penetration testing framework written in Go that uses artificial intelligence agents to perform reconnaissance, discover vulnerabilities, exploit systems, escalate privileges, and steal data with little human intervention.
Rather than using its own AI model, the framework integrates with external large language models (LLMs), including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, and Kimi.
Attackers provide their goals and tasks to ARTEX, which converts them into commands executed by specialized AI agents. This allows them to automate intrusion activities and target multiple organizations simultaneously.
The FBI says the framework is particularly effective at identifying vulnerabilities in overlooked systems, including partner portals, employee applications, legacy services, and third-party integrations.
While these automated attacks can generate large volumes of suspicious traffic that trigger security alerts, their speed can leave defenders with little time to respond before attackers breach a system.
ARTEX was originally released on GitHub in July 2026 by a developer known as Autumn-27, who removed the repository on October 8 after reports emerged that threat actors were abusing the framework.
However, the FBI says the framework remains available through community forks, archived copies, localized versions, and a commercial edition called ARTEX PRO.
As of early November, researchers had identified more than 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles, with the actual number of deployments believed to be significantly higher.
The FBI's 13-page advisory includes indicators of compromise associated with known ARTEX campaigns, including IP addresses, command-and-control infrastructure, and suspicious network activity.
Separately, cybersecurity researcher MalwareMustDie released an open-source ARTEX detection signature pack on Friday to help defenders identify attacks involving the framework.
The detection pack includes rules and indicators for various security monitoring and threat detection tools, covering suspicious network requests, identity abuse, cloud activity, malicious files, and automated attack patterns.
The researcher also published a detection playbook that categorizes indicators by confidence level, warning that IP addresses and other infrastructure indicators can become outdated or generate false positives.
Organizations are urged to secure internet-facing applications, restrict access to cloud administration interfaces, review application permissions and authentication logs, and implement rate limits on sensitive APIs.
The bureau also recommends monitoring for unusual bursts of automated requests, suspicious cloud activity, unexpected credential or privilege changes, and large data transfers.
The FBI cautions that IP addresses listed in the IOCs may have changed since the attacks occurred.
Organizations that identify suspicious activity associated with ARTEX are encouraged to report their findings to the FBI or its Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).
The advisory highlights several previously reported cyberattacks involving ARTEX, including the October ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain attack that allowed hackers to gain unauthorized access to Microsoft 365 customer environments.
The attack compromised application identities used by ConnectWise's cloud backup service, formerly known as SkyKick Cloud Backup, allowing attackers to authenticate to customer tenants using permissions previously granted to the applications.
At the time, cybersecurity firm Huntress reported identifying at least 162 compromised tenants.
In an investigation published in October, Microsoft attributed the campaign to a China-state-aligned threat actor tracked as Storm-0940, which used ARTEX to accelerate reconnaissance, password spraying, and abuse of cloud application permissions.
After compromising ConnectWise application identities, the attackers used ARTEX to attempt authentication against more than 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 tenants, with some intrusions progressing to credential modifications and attempts to establish persistent access.
The FBI also referenced attacks against South Korean financial institutions that exposed personal information belonging to approximately 67,000 people.
In that campaign, a Chinese-speaking threat actor combined ARTEX with Claude Code agents to attack multiple banks, including Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, and Hana Bank.
Researchers at CrowdStrike discovered the attacker's exposed infrastructure, which contained ARTEX configuration files, Claude Code session histories, and other records documenting the intrusions.
In a separate investigation, South Korean police arrested seven suspects linked to attacks against more than 90 organizations, with ARTEX reportedly used in most of the intrusions.
Authorities said the gang stole approximately 8.2 million data records from organizations including hospitals, educational institutions, and businesses.
More recently, CrowdStrike reported that a Chinese cyberespionage group tracked as Vapor Panda used ARTEX in automated attacks targeting more than 200 organizations across 14 countries.
The campaign compromised at least nine organizations, with AI agents performing reconnaissance, exploiting vulnerabilities, deploying web shells, stealing credentials, and pursuing different attack paths when initial attempts failed.

zh_title: 台积电员工数据泄露与云提供商有关
summary: 与云提供商相关的台积电员工数据泄露 与云提供商相关的台积电员工数据泄露 与云提供商相关的台积电员工数据泄露 台积电 (TSMC) 证实，在威胁行为者将据称从该公司窃取的 6.9GB 信息进行拍卖后，个人员工数据已在网上泄露。这家科技巨头表示，该事件影响了现任和前任员工，但不会影响其运营或客户。该公司对泄露的信息进行了核实，并确认其与“存储在某公司系统服务中的数据”相符。
content:
台积电员工数据泄露与云提供商有关
台积电员工数据泄露与云提供商有关
台积电员工数据泄露与云提供商有关
台积电 (TSMC) 证实，一名威胁行为者将据称从该公司窃取的 6.9GB 信息进行拍卖后，员工个人数据已在网上泄露。
这家科技巨头表示，该事件影响了现任和前任员工，但不会影响其运营或客户。
该公司核实了泄露的信息，并确认其与“云服务提供商的系统服务中存储的数据”相匹配，表明存在外部泄露。
台积电是全球最大的合约芯片制造商，为苹果和英伟达等公司制造先进处理器和其他半导体。
去年，该公司出货了约1500万片12英寸等效晶圆，年收入为1224亿美元。
台积电的调查发现，泄露的信息与其使用的云服务提供商中存储的数据相匹配，表明其自身基础设施之外存在漏洞。
该公司目前正在通知受影响的员工并提供必要的支持，同时还聘请第三方网络安全公司来帮助管理这种情况。
台积电在向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交的文件中表示：“台积电发现，我们的一些现任和前任员工数据未经授权就在外部网站上公开。”
该公司补充说：“目前，我们没有发现任何证据表明台积电的系统受到了损害。”
11 月 8 日，有人使用别名“SmithBianl”在黑客论坛上泄露了一个文本文件，其中包含据称从台积电窃取的 499 行信息。该攻击者声称该文件是包含 46,000 条员工记录的 6.9GB 数据集的样本。
帖子称，泄露的信息包括台积电员工的身份证号码、地址、联系方式和银行信息。
SmithBianl 提供了数据拍卖，起价为 3 BTC（约 65,000 美元）。
在没有买家的情况下，他们警告称，数据将在一周内免费泄露，并将第一个截止日期定为 11 月 15 日。
BleepingComputer 已联系台积电，询问他们是否已与威胁行为者进行接触，以及是否计划向黑客付费以防止其员工数据完全公开泄露。

【原文 English Original】
TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) confirmed that personal employee data has been leaked online after a threat actor put 6.9GB of information allegedly stolen from the company up for auction.
The technology giant said the incident affected current and former employees but doesn’t impact its operations or customers.
The company verified the leaked information and confirmed that it matched "data stored in the system services of a cloud service provider," indicating an external breach.
TSMC is the world’s largest contract chipmaker, manufacturing advanced processors and other semiconductors for companies such as Apple and Nvidia.
Last year, it shipped approximately 15 million 12-inch-equivalent wafers and generated $122.4 billion in annual revenue.
TSMC's investigation found that the leaked information matched data stored in a cloud service provider it uses, pointing to a breach outside its own infrastructure.
The company is now notifying impacted staff and providing the necessary support, while also engaging a third-party cybersecurity firm to help manage the situation.
“TSMC has found that some of our current and former employee data was made available on an external website without authorization,” TSMC says in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
“Currently, we have found no evidence that TSMC’s systems have been compromised,” the company added.
On November 8, someone using the alias ‘SmithBianl’ leaked on a hacker forum a text file containing 499 rows of information allegedly stolen from TSMC. The actor claimed the file was a sample of a 6.9GB dataset containing 46,000 employee records.
According to the post, the leaked information included TSMC employees' national ID numbers, addresses, contact details, and banking information.
SmithBianl offered the data for auction, with bidding starting at 3 BTC (approximately $65,000).
In the absence of a buyer, they warned that the data would be leaked for free in one week, setting the first deadline to November 15.
BleepingComputer has contacted TSMC to ask whether they have engaged with the threat actor and whether they planned to pay the hackers to prevent a full public leak of their employees’ data.
A spokesperson declined to comment at this stage.

title: Taiwan lawmaker wanted by police in China closes gap in race for Taipei mayor
zh_title: 被中国警方通缉的台湾议员缩小台北市长竞选差距
summary: 一名被中国警方通缉的台湾议员正在竞选台北市市长，这场竞选在国民党的中心地带进行，这场竞选出人意料地势均力敌，国民党倾向于与北京建立更密切的关系。 2026 年 11 月 15 日，台湾总统赖清德（左）和民进党台北市市长候选人沉宝阳（又名普马沉）在台北竞选期间举起礼仪剑。照片：郑宇辰/法新社。夜市、寺庙和车队正在为 11 月 28 日选举进行竞选活动，选举将决定市长、地方法官和其他职位的竞选
content:
一名被中国警方通缉的台湾议员正在竞选台北市市长，这场竞选在国民党的中心地带进行，这场竞选出人意料地势均力敌，国民党倾向于与北京建立更密切的关系。 2026 年 11 月 15 日，台湾总统赖清德（左）和民进党台北市市长候选人沉宝阳（又名普马沉）在台北竞选期间举起礼仪剑。照片：郑宇辰/法新社。夜市、寺庙和车队正在为 11 月 28 日的选举进行竞选活动，该选举将决定全岛民主政体的市长、地方法官和其他职位的竞选。 2022 年，国民党赢得了台湾 22 个市县中的 14 个席位（包括台北），而赖清德领导的民进党则获得了 5 个席位。 44 岁的台北民进党候选人普马·沉 (Puma Shen) 正在寻求推翻长期以来被认为是安全的国民党职位，成为近 30 年来第一位民进党首都市长。沉在 2024 年成为立法委员，他几乎没有机会击败 47 岁的国民党现任议员蒋万安，后者被视为台湾历史最悠久的政党的后起之秀和未来的总统候选人。但最近的选民调查显示，沉正接近甚至略微领先蒋介石。
另请参阅：台湾指控香港居民雇佣 4 名人员监视批评中国的议员。沉在台湾立法院附近的办公室接受法新社采访时表示，“我始终相信自己能够获胜”。沉在台湾议会附近的办公室接受法新社采访时表示，他一直直言不讳地谈论中国的影响力和虚假信息。沉因涉嫌犯罪“分裂活动”正在接受中国警方的调查，并被禁止入境。沉说，他在选民中越来越受欢迎——他的竞选团队将其称为“洋流”，这是对他名字最后一个字符的戏剧——部分原因是他愿意回答他们的问题。 “我认为这就是民主的本质，”沉说，他利用演讲台和社交媒体直接与当地人接触。蒋的团队拒绝了法新社采访市长的请求。上海市市长龚正与台北市长蒋万安在2023上海台北城市论坛上握手。照片：台北市政府。前国民党顾问曾伟业表示，两位候选人的性格和政治风格截然不同。他说，蒋是一位“正派的政治家”，但“在表达自己的观点时非常保守”，而沉则更“直言不讳”，更适合社交媒体。北京关注的选民调查还显示，台湾最大城市、国民党另一个据点新北市的市长竞选可能会出现重大意外。
在2028年总统选举之前，失去台北和新北市对国民党来说将是一个打击，届时国民党将寻求阻止民进党获得第四个任期。赖政府中的一些人担心，国民党在这两个重要城市的失利可能会让与该党关系密切、关注选举的中国领导人感到尴尬。中国国家主席习近平今年四月会见了国民党主席郑丽媛，她是十年来第一位访问中国的国民党领导人，这被视为对她作为党主席的认可。国民党主席郑立文于 2026 年 4 月会见中国领导人习近平。照片：中国共产党。民进党在台北和新北市的胜利可能对北京来说“看起来非常令人担忧”，因为这将表明该党可以获得以前被视为国民党轻松获胜的席位。

【原文 English Original】
A Taiwanese lawmaker wanted by police in China is running for Taipei mayor in an unexpectedly close race in the heartland of the Kuomintang party, which favours closer ties with Beijing. Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te (L) and Taipei mayoral candidate Shen Pao-yang, also known as Puma Shen, of the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) raise a ceremonial sword during an election campaign in Taipei on November 15, 2026. Photo: Cheng Yu-chen/AFP. Campaigning in night markets, temples and motorcades is underway for the November 28 elections that will decide races for mayors, magistrates and other posts across the island democracy. The Kuomintang party (KMT) won 14 of Taiwan’s 22 cities and counties — including Taipei — in a huge victory in 2022, while President Lai Ching-te’s Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) secured five seats. Puma Shen, the 44-year-old DPP candidate in Taipei, is seeking to flip what has long been considered a safe KMT post and become the first DPP mayor of the capital in nearly 30 years. Shen, who became a lawmaker in 2024, had been given little chance of beating KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an, 47, who is seen as a rising star and future presidential candidate for Taiwan’s oldest party. But recent voter surveys show Shen closing in on, or even slightly ahead, of Chiang. See also: Taiwan accuses Hong Kong residents of hiring 4 people to spy on lawmaker critical of China “I always believe I can win,” Shen told AFP in an interview at his office near Taiwan’s parliament, where he has been outspoken about Chinese influence and disinformation. Shen is under investigation by police in China for alleged criminal “separatist activities” and is barred from entering the country. Shen said his growing popularity among voters — which his campaign has dubbed an “Ocean Current”, in a play on the last character of his name — is partly due to his willingness to answer their questions. “I think that’s the essence of democracy,” said Shen, who has used soapboxes and social media to engage directly with locals. Chiang’s team declined AFP’s request for an interview with the mayor. Shanghai mayor Gong Zheng and Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an shaking hands at the 2023 Shanghai–Taipei City Forum. Photo: Taipei City Government. Albert Tzeng, a former KMT adviser, said the two candidates have very different personalities and political styles. Chiang is a “decent politician” but “very conservative in articulating his view”, while Shen is more “outspoken” and better suited to social media, he said. Beijing watching Voter surveys also show a potential major upset in the mayoral race in New Taipei City, Taiwan’s largest city and another KMT stronghold. Losing Taipei and New Taipei City would be a blow for the KMT ahead of the 2028 presidential election when the party will seek to prevent the DPP from securing a fourth term. Some in Lai’s government worry that KMT losses in the two key cities could embarrass Chinese leaders who have close ties with the party and will be watching the election. Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Kuomintang chairwoman Cheng Li-wun in April, the first KMT leader to visit China in a decade, in what was seen as his endorsement of her as head of the party. KMT chair Cheng Li-wun meets Chinese leader Xi Jinping in April 2026. Photo: Communist Party of China. A DPP victory in Taipei and New Taipei City might “look very concerning” to Beijing because it would show the party can gain seats previously seen as easy wins for the KMT, said Lev Nachman, a political science professor at National Taiwan University. A poor performance by the KMT would also likely increase pressure on Cheng, whose strident pro-Beijing stance has angered many in her own party, to step down. Most KMT candidates have kept their distance from Cheng during their campaigns and after the elections there will be a “very ugly struggle”, Tzeng predicted. “There are many people who believe if Cheng Li-wun stays in power, the KMT will have zero chance in 2028.” Local issues Analysts cautioned that local elections should not be seen as a predictor of how people might vote in the presidential race, with history showing repeatedly that it can be the reverse. “The things they (voters) weigh in local elections differ from what they weigh in national-level elections,” Hsiao Yi-ching, director of the Election Study Center at National Chengchi University, told AFP. “Local elections should be relatively less affected by cross-strait tensions and geopolitical or international political factors.” Shen and Chiang have avoided talking about China during their campaigns, focusing instead on local issues such as urban renewal, transportation, childcare and artificial intelligence. Campaign posters for Chiang Wan-an and Puma Shen. Photo: Chiang Wan-an and Puma Shen, via Facebook. Lo Hui-fen, a 67-year-old retiree and supporter of Chiang, said he thought the mayor was “excellent” and had achieved a lot during his first term. “To me, he is like the son next door,” Lo said at a night market where Chiang was holding a campaign event. “He’s very approachable and willing to get things done.” Shen supporter Jamie Cheng, 35, said the DPP candidate made her feel like he was listening. “I can have a formal exchange with him,” Cheng, a digital designer, told AFP at a rally for the opening of Shen’s campaign office. “It feels like my voice is being heard.”

title: Hong Kong police activate facial recognition across AI-enabled CCTV network, as police chief says tools ‘won’t be abused’
zh_title: 香港警方通过人工智能闭路电视网络启动面部识别，警察局长表示工具“不会被滥用”
summary: 香港警务处宣布将于周一在其监控摄像系统中启动面部识别工具。该措施是一项耗资 40 亿港元的扩大人工智能闭路电视网络计划的一部分。 SmartView 摄像头馈送。资料图：香港警务处。警务处处长 Joe Chow 周日告诉 TVB，该技术将在其 SmartView 网络上推广。 “我们所有的调查工具都有制衡的要求，这样就不会被滥用……我们理解很多人可能会担心这一点，所以这是我们的常规做法，”周先生用粤语说。
content:
香港警务处宣布将于周一在其监控摄像系统中启动面部识别工具。该措施是一项耗资 40 亿港元的扩大人工智能闭路电视网络计划的一部分。 SmartView 摄像头馈送。资料图：香港警务处。警务处处长 Joe Chow 周日告诉 TVB，该技术将在其 SmartView 网络上推广。据香港电台报道，周先生用粤语说：“我们所有的调查工具都有制衡的要求，这样就不会被滥用……我们知道很多人可能会担心这一点，所以这是我们的常规做法。”他补充说，这些工具主要用于处理失踪人员或刑事案件：“该系统不会随便使用——我相信这不是公众所期望的。”周说，他理解公众的担忧，但闭路电视系统已经被用来侦破抢劫案件。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在周六的香港警察学院结业游行上，他表示，部署面部识别功能的目的是为了更好地保护守法居民，并起到威慑犯罪活动的作用。另请参阅：香港警方今年可能在闭路电视摄像机中添加面部识别功能，作为 40 亿港元扩张计划的一部分。当被记者问到口罩或伪装是否会阻碍该系统时，周表示，警方不会透露技术和操作细节。
不过，他补充说，隐蔽方法无法与警方的能力相抗衡。 SmartView系统扩展 自2024年推出以来，SmartView系统已安装在犯罪黑点和人口密集地区，警方声称该系统已帮助破获了1,659起谋杀、伤人和抢劫案件。该政府主导的计划涉及约 5,000 个警察摄像头和 6,000 个第三方源。去年施政报告中提出的第二阶段计划包括安装 20,000 个摄像头，到 2028 年在全市实现 60,000 个摄像头网络。上个月，安全部门负责人 Chris Tang 表示，警方正与私人购物中心讨论将摄像头纳入 SmartView 系统的最后阶段。他没有透露涉及的商场名称。 “我们看到，在一些没有闭路电视的地方，公众不愿意参观，因为那里很危险，人们担心成为犯罪的受害者，”他用粤语说。警方网站指出 SmartView 计划有四个目的，第一个是维护国家安全。它还列出了犯罪的预防、侦查和调查，维护公共秩序和安全，以及防止生命和财产伤害。

【原文 English Original】
The Hong Kong Police Force has announced that it will activate facial recognition tools across its surveillance camera system on Monday. The measure is part of a HK$4 billion plan to expand the AI-enabled CCTV network. SmartView camera feeds. File Photo: HKPF. Police Commissioner Joe Chow told TVB on Sunday that the technology would be rolled out across its SmartView network. “All of our investigation tools have the requirement of check and balance, so that they won’t be abused… We understand that many people may be concerned about this, so it’s our routine practice,” Chow said in Cantonese, according to RTHK. He added that the tools would mostly be used to deal with missing persons or criminal cases: “The system will not be used casually – I believe this is not what the public expects.” Chow said he understood public concerns, but the CCTV system had already been used to solve robbery cases. A CCTV camera in Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. At a Hong Kong Police College passing-out parade on Saturday, he said the deployment of facial recognition features was aimed at better protecting law-abiding residents and acting as a deterrent against criminal activity. See also: Hong Kong police may add facial recognition to CCTV cameras this year as part of HK$4 billion expansion plan When asked by reporters if face masks or disguises could thwart the system, Chow said the force would refrain from disclosing technical and operational details. However, he added that concealment methods would be no match against the capabilities of the police. SmartView system expansion Since its launch in 2024, the SmartView system has been installed across crime blackspots and dense population areas, with the police claiming that it has helped solve 1,659 cases including murder, wounding and robbery. The government-led programme involves around 5,000 police cameras and 6,000 third-party feeds. The second phase of the scheme, laid out in last year’s Policy Address, involves the installation of 20,000 more cameras to achieve a network of 60,000 across the city by 2028. Last month, security chief Chris Tang said the police force was in the final stages of discussion with private shopping centres to bring their cameras into the SmartView system. He did not name the malls involved. “[W]e see that in some places without CCTV, members of the public do not want to visit because they are dangerous and people fear becoming victims of crime,” he said in Cantonese. The police website states four purposes for the SmartView scheme, with the first being safeguarding national security. It also lists the prevention, detection and investigation of crimes, the preservation of public order and safety, and the prevention of injury to life and property.

2026 年 11 月 15 日，澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞（中）和菲律宾国防部长特奥多罗·吉尔伯托在菲律宾马尼拉签署防务合作协议后合影。
菲律宾和澳大利亚昨天签署了一项防务协议，该协议将促进两国之间的军事合作，特别是通过简化联合军事活动涉及的官僚程序。
防务合作协议（DCA）以多项现有防务协议为基础，是在一艘停靠在马尼拉的澳大利亚海军舰艇上举行的仪式上签署的。总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞在仪式后表示，该协议将加强军事基础设施的发展、海洋意识和信息共享。
他说：“这些活动将有助于使我们的地区更加安全、更加繁荣。” “我们正在与菲律宾和我们的区域伙伴一起加强海上复原力和安全，这有助于巩固该地区的和平、稳定和繁荣。”
菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗补充说，新协议将减少执行访问部队地位协议（SOVFA）所涉及的繁文缛节，该协议管理菲律宾和澳大利亚临时访问对方领土时军事人员的部署。据路透社报道，特奥多罗对记者表示：“做一件事不再需要 100 个步骤，而现在只需要 10 个步骤。”
他表示，这一安排将为两国海上、空中和地面部队以及人道主义和灾难应对方面更密切的合作铺平道路。它还将加强菲律宾的“可信威慑姿态”，包括在南海部分地区，中国近年来增加了入侵南海的频率和强度。
最近的紧张局势集中在吕宋岛以西的斯卡伯勒浅滩和南沙群岛的仁爱礁，马尼拉在一艘搁浅的军舰上驻扎着一小支占领军。这引发了一系列危险的冲突，中国海警冲撞菲律宾民用和海警船只，并用高压水枪浇水。在某些情况下，菲律宾人和中国人甚至发生肢体冲突。
中国日益增长的压力产生了可预见的效果，促使菲律宾与同样对中国日益增长的海上力量感到担忧的伙伴和盟友结成更紧密的联盟。
澳大利亚是该组织中最古老的成员之一，于 2007 年与菲律宾签署了《SOVFA》——这是除 1998 年菲律宾和美国签署的《访问部队协议》之外的任何国家中第一个此类协议。

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese (center) and Philippine Defense Secretary Teodoro Gilberto pose for a photo after the signing of the Defense Cooperation Agreement in Manila, Philippines, Nov. 15, 2026.
The Philippines and Australia signed a defense pact yesterday that will boost military cooperation between the two nations, in particular by streamlining the bureaucratic processes involved in joint military activities.
The Defense Cooperation Agreement (DCA), which builds on a number of existing defense accords, was signed in a ceremony on board an Australian naval vessel docked in Manila. The pact will enhance the development of military infrastructure and maritime awareness and information sharing, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said after the ceremony.
“These activities will contribute to making our region more safe, more secure and more prosperous,” he said. “Together with the Philippines and our regional partners we are strengthening maritime resilience and security that helps underpin a peaceful, stable and prosperous region.”
Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro added that the new agreement would cut back the red tape involved in the implementation of the Status of Visiting Forces Agreement (SOVFA), which governs the deployment of Philippine and Australian military personnel while temporarily visiting the other country’s territory. “Rather than 100 steps to do ​a single thing, it will just now take 10,” Teodoro told reporters, ​as per Reuters.
He said the ⁠arrangement would pave the way for closer cooperation of the two nations’ maritime, air, and land ​forces, as well as humanitarian and disaster response. It would also bolster the Philippines’ “credible deterrence posture,” ​including in its portions of the South China Sea, into which China has in recent years increased both the frequency and intensity of its incursions.
Recent tensions have centered on Scarborough Shoal, a reef due west of Luzon, and Second Thomas Shoal in the Spratly Islands, where Manila maintains a small occupying force aboard a grounded warship. This has prompted a series of dangerous confrontations in which the China Coast Guard has rammed Philippine civilian and coast guard vessels and doused them with high-pressure water cannons. In some cases, Philippine and Chinese personal have even exchanged physical blows.
The growing Chinese pressure has had the predictable effect of pushing the Philippines into closer alignment of partners and allies who share its concerns about China’s growing maritime power.
Australia is among the oldest members of this group, having signed the SOVFA with the Philippines in 2007 – the first agreement of its sort of any nation aside from the Visiting Forces Agreement signed between the Philippines and U.S. in 1998. Similar agreements have since been signed with Japan (July 2024), New Zealand (April 2025), Canada (November 2025), and France (March 2026), with negotiations also underway with the United Kingdom.
These agreements have provided the legal scaffolding for a marked increase in joint maritime and coast guard patrols and military exercises known as Maritime Cooperative Activities (MCAs), which now take place regularly in the waters around the Philippines The 20th MCA was held between the Philippines, U.S., and Canada in the Sulu Sea in mid-September.
The growing cooperation has also taken “minilateral” form. The past few years have seen the emergence of a defense bloc of four nations – Australia, the U.S., the Philippines and Japan – nicknamed “the Squad,” which is working together to bolster the Philippines’ defensive capability in an attempt to counter China’s maritime influence in the South and East China seas.
After a meeting of “Squad” defense chiefs in Cebu on October 28, the four nations announced that they would have agreed to establish a coordination hub in the Philippines and to synchronize efforts to strengthen the nation’s defenses.
During their meeting, the Squad defense chiefs expressed their “serious concerns about the situations in the East China Sea and the South China Sea.” They also raised opposition to “any unilateral actions, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability.”
In recent years, Australia has also invested in defense infrastructure at a series of bases across the Philippines, and also providing various forms of support for the Philippine Coast Guard.
The signing of the DCA took place as the Philippines opened the 49th ASEAN Summit and related meetings in Manila, during which the South China Sea disputes were again likely to feature prominently – as they did at the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting in Cebu last month.
In a related announcement yesterday, Philippine Foreign Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro told the press that China and ASEAN had been unable to ‌conclude negotiations on a long-delayed Code of Conduct (COC) for the South China Sea under the Philippines’ chairmanship this year.
The Code is intended to reduce the risk of conflict in the important waterway, where China’s expansive “nine-dash line” maritime claim clashes with those of four ASEAN member states: Vietnam, Malaysia, the Philippines, and Brunei.
The Philippines had pledged to complete the negotiations during its chairmanship but Lazaro said that several key issues remain unresolved, including questions over whether the Code would ​be legally binding.
“There is no ⁠conclusion yet,” she said, adding that “the ASEAN countries plus China have also different views on how things are.”
In a separate statement about the Code, the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said that the two sides had reached agreement on “over 80 percent of the paragraphs of the draft COC.” The DFA said that the parties to the Code “agree to continue to work constructively, with a view to concluding the negotiations on an effective and substantive COC at the earliest possible time.”

Global outcry over Joshua Wong’s 10-year sentence
Long prison terms in Hong Kong and Macao deepen fears for freedom of expression
Pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong addresses a crowd after his release from jail in Hong Kong in June 2019. He later spent six consecutive years in prison on convictions including unlawful assembly, subversion and conspiracy to collude with foreign forces. On Nov. 5, a Hong Kong court sentenced Wong to 10 more years in prison for national security offenses. | Lam Yik Fei / The New York Times
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Ten countries, including the United States, Japan and the United Kingdom, have condemned Hong Kong’s decision to sentence pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to 10 years in prison, while the European Union has deplored a separate 12½-year sentence imposed on former Macao pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam-san. The unusually strong international response reflects growing alarm over the erosion of civil liberties and the rule of law in the former British and Portuguese colonies, which increasingly resemble mainland China in their repression of dissent.
Wong, who turned 30 last month, was sentenced Nov. 5 on a charge of “conspiracy to collude with foreign forces.” He had already spent six years in detention and was originally expected to be released in January 2027 after his conviction in the case involving 47 pro-democracy figures arrested over their participation in a 2020 primary election. Wong pleaded guilty, apparently expecting a more lenient sentence.
The following day, Au, 69, received a 12½-year sentence for “subversion of state power” in Macao. His sentencing took place in a closed-door hearing. Wong will be 40 when released; Au will be over 80.
