Is India Extending Its Control Over Islamic Practice In Kashmir?
Washington has spent years debating the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in nuclear command and control, and agonizing over the military implications of China-U.S. AI competition. It has spent far less time asking a different question: how will North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s deterrence calculus change if he believes the United States is on the verge of obtaining a powerful, enduring advantage in artificial general intelligence?
Artificial general intelligence (AGI) – defined as powerful intelligence matching human performance across cognitive tasks – could further destabilize nuclear deterrence relationships that are already deteriorating. Weaker, non-AGI powers could become especially problematic. North Korea’s nuclear posture is already on a hair trigger. If the United States obtains AGI or AGI-like capabilities, Pyongyang could adopt an aggressive “use it or lose it” mentality because it fears a first strike that eradicates its nuclear weapons capabilities and decapitates its leadership.
Critically, the United States’ actual acquisition of AGI and the subsequent development of deterrence-nullifying capabilities matters less than North Korea’s perceptions of U.S. capabilities and intent. Because Pyongyang has adopted an aggressive nuclear posture and espouses such a critical, paranoid view of U.S. intentions, the situation could spiral even before AGI capabilities are operational. More attention should therefore be paid to how AGI could upset asymmetric deterrence equilibria, especially vis-à-vis Pyongyang.
If AGI takeoff truly unlocks exponential growth, a cascade of technological breakthroughs could spur unprecedented economic growth and expansion in military capabilities that some have termed agentic warfare. Under this scenario, an AGI-capable power could rapidly erode, if not eliminate, the second strike capabilities of a non-AGI power. This technological leap would amplify the unfortunate psychological tendency to become more risk-prone when facing losses, called prospect theory.
Accordingly, under AGI takeoff, non-AGI nuclear weapons powers, especially the weaker ones, will likely fear a near-future wherein they will be unable to deter the AGI power. They could therefore adopt a more aggressive posture. Of course, this isn’t the only rational reaction, but for reasons we will describe later, we think North Korea is much more likely to respond with extra aggression than it is to seek refuge through survivability, concealment, and arms control negotiations. Moreover, if recursive self-improvement delivers artificial superintelligence (ASI), defined as capabilities exceeding any human, the stakes will become much higher and nuclear decision-making timelines will become even more compressed.
AGI consequences, timelines, and diffusion remain a subject of debate, and key AI breakthroughs may be a business cycle or more away, but the balance of evidence suggests huge capability increases are possible. If scaling laws continue to hold, capabilities will keep rising: announced U.S. AI computing capacity is projected to increase by 239 percent this year alone, according to Federal Reserve staff calculations based on Epoch AI data. By 2030, planned U.S. AI compute would be roughly 35 times mid-2025 levels.
While tech CEOs and investors are incentivized to hype AI advances, models are undeniably improving, and at an impressive rate; the newest models are even proving adept at operating in the physical world. For better and for worse, AI software and hardware capabilities are advancing rapidly. Even artificial intelligence experts themselves have expressed surprise at the pace of innovation and warned of the dangers of unrestricted development.
Strategic deterrence nullification would likely lag AGI by many years, but AI timelines are advancing far faster than most expected. North Korea’s force posture is already changing and new command-and-control safeguards – including human-in-the-loop commitments – may take years to agree upon and implement.
AGI attainment would usher in considerable geopolitical disruptions, including altering the nuclear balance-of-power. China and Russia are of special importance in any AGI scenario. China is a peer competitor of the United States, including in AI, and it possesses the world’s third largest nuclear arsenal; Russia possesses the world’s largest nuclear weapon arsenal (by volume) and continues to face off against the United States in Cold War-style proxy conflict. Either competitor could be incentivized to act aggressively if the U.S. is first to approach AGI attainment.
Nevertheless, the gravest AGI-related dangers may come from less-capable nuclear powers, especially North Korea. That’s because Pyongyang has adopted a uniquely aggressive and decentralized form of nuclear command and control, has an aggressive nuclear doctrine, suffers from severe technical and even geographic disadvantages, and it maintains a paranoid disposition towards the United States. Faced with the prospect of losing second strike capability, it could therefore choose to adopt an even riskier posture or operationalize half-baked tech into its nuclear command, control, and communications before the United States crosses the AGI threshold.
Nuclear stability requires mutual vulnerability. China and Russia are more likely to continue to hold the U.S. hostage via threat of retaliation even if the U.S. obtains AGI first; for North Korea, that is much less likely.
AGI Takeoff, or Perceived Takeoff, Upends Conventional and Strategic Military Calculations
If AGI takeoff occurs, its technological, economic, and military consequences will be extremely hard to forecast. Physical constraints and hardware bottlenecks, including in critical minerals, could slow the transformation of software breakthroughs into weapons. Still, powerful AI could rapidly deliver unprecedented economic and technological capacity, which would then translate into military capabilities, including early warning, detection, targeting, and delivery. These capabilities could credibly threaten other states’ second-strike forces.
As the decision window shrinks, mutual vulnerability – the foundation of a stable deterrence relationship – will erode. Given the dangers of facing an AGI-empowered rival, and their own weak monitoring and verification capabilities, non-AGI powers like Pyongyang will watch anxiously for signs that an adversary’s AGI attainment could unlock the potential for a decapitation strike that wipes out their leadership and nuclear capabilities in one fell swoop.
In this scenario, facing rapidly deteriorating strategic options, a state could be motivated to automate nuclear retaliation. They might hope that the dead man’s hand would serve as a final guarantor of deterrence. But as human operators are pulled further out of the nuclear decision-making process, the ethical and practical problems will begin to multiply. History has proven that humans are the last best defense against needless escalation. That was the case in 1983 when a Soviet early warning system erroneously signaled an incoming U.S. intercontinental ballistic missile. Using his knowledge of the faulty system and U.S. strategy, Lieutenant Colonel Stanislav Petrov deduced that the warning was a false positive. He was right: the system’s satellites misread sunlight reflecting off clouds.
In addition, North Korea – and other non-AGI actors – might seek to establish deterrence via other asymmetric methods, such as pre-positioning chemical and biological weapons or developing new, AI-enabled variants. North Korea is thought to have a substantial inventory of both chemical and biological weapons, and it might lean on these capabilities if it fears its nuclear deterrent is compromised.
To limit near-term biological risks from Pyongyang, both Washington and Beijing should closely examine the AI-biology nexus, an asymmetrical threat that North Korea might find compelling to develop if it believed a rival was on the cusp of AGI acquisition. Limiting the risk of North Korea – or other state and non-state actors – may require constraining the publicly-accessible biological capabilities of future releases of large language models. Unsafeguarded models, known as open-weight models, pose the most severe risks. As unsafeguarded models become more capable, virtually anyone can access powerful, unconstrained AI by removing safeguards with relatively little compute.
North Korea is already likely operating unsafeguarded models to exploit zero-day vulnerabilities, as the $6 billion Binance hack suggests. Given the growing risks of AI-designed viruses, including from Pyongyang, Beijing and Washington should have candid conversations about the desirability of diffusing powerful AI capabilities in biology.
North Korea Is Uniquely Vulnerable and Aggressive
Unlike China or Russia, which have large nuclear arsenals, mature intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities, and demonstrated technological ability to innovate, North Korea’s vulnerability and its aggressive posture may render it the most dangerous nuclear actor in an AGI sprint scenario. Furthermore, unlike China or Russia, countries that can rely on second-strike deterrents due to their deep interiors and nuclear-armed submarines, North Korea lacks a credibly survivable nuclear submarine deterrent.
Finally, North Korea’s own eagerness to adopt AI-enabled weapons will color its perception of adversary intent and the threat posed by AGI. The nuclear deterrence equilibrium on the Korean Peninsula is already fragile; inviting one more destabilizing element may be the straw that breaks the camel’s back.
North Korea’s military is embracing AI with a speed that suggests it is throwing caution to the wind. In 2024, the General Staff Department of the Korean People’s Army created an Electronic Warfare and AI Operation Command to develop and adopt “AI-based electronic warfare support systems.” In August 2025, the Korean People’s Army issued orders to its Strategic Force to “integrate AI-based unified management systems for storing, operating, and commanding nuclear weapons, as well as launching nuclear counterattacks,” according to Daily NK. At the Ninth Party Congress in February of this year, North Korea announced additional plans to integrate AI into its civil and military systems. Since then, even more developments have been announced.
Leader Kim Jong Un himself jumped behind the wheel of a mobile rocket launcher, claiming that the nuclear-capable 600-mm multiple rocket launcher (KN-25) features artificial intelligence in its guidance systems. One month later, Kim oversaw a test of AI-enabled attack and reconnaissance drones, saying, “unmanned equipment and artificial intelligence should be top-prioritized… in modernizing the armed forces.” In May, North Korean media claimed that the military tested a tactical cruise missile that utilizes artificial intelligence for target acquisition and terminal guidance. Despite this appetite for integrating AI across military technologies, limitations in hardware, data, and infrastructure will likely constrain the rollout. These limitations could also produce defects that imperil safeguards meant to stop an unintentional escalation spiral.
Further aggravating the situation, North Korea’s nuclear doctrine is uniquely aggressive and opaque. The country’s rubber stamp parliament passed legislation in 2022 that legitimizes preemptive nuclear attacks under certain conditions. The North will launch a nuclear attack “automatically and immediately” if Kim’s command is threatened, if “a fatal military attack” on critical targets is imminent, or if needed to reclaim “the initiative in war.” The law also outlined a delegative command authority: “Rather than await direct orders from Kim Jong Un, field commanders may now follow predetermined launch plans to release nuclear weapons.” These doctrinal reforms were reinforced by a 2026 constitutional revision that codified the decentralized command authority. Combined with a surge in the production and forward deployment of tactical nuclear weapons, these changes add coherence and credibility to Kim’s first-use strategy, which aims to achieve a maximum deterrence effect through aggression and ambiguity. However, the blurry red lines and threats of preemption are risky and escalatory.
An AGI scenario could lead to further brinksmanship. As Keir A. Lieber and Daryl G. Press noted in a 2017 analysis, “The New Era of Counterforce,” states facing wealthy, technologically advanced adversaries will find it “increasingly difficult to secure their arsenals” as advances in sensors, data processing, and AI erode the conditions that have historically protected second-strike forces.
Pyongyang cannot rule out that an AGI-powered United States will develop next-generation technologies, such as airborne directed energy weapons, highly effective anti-ballistic missile defense, and orbital and sub-orbital weapons. Pyongyang’s weak early warning and intelligence capabilities will amplify the leadership’s fear that its second strike has been rendered moot, especially given its unique vulnerabilities. Nor can Washington easily reassure North Korea: even if the United States integrates AI cautiously into its own nuclear command, control, and communications and is transparent about human-in-the-loop safeguards, a leadership this distrustful could conclude that the AGI moment has arrived and act accordingly.
It is possible that, faced with such daunting odds, North Korea could choose a path of survivability, restraint, and even reconciliation. That would be a rational reaction to this newfound unfavorable position. However, given Pyongyang’s nuclear posture, its historical record, and the leadership’s consistent commitment to robust nuclear capabilities, it is much more likely that Pyongyang will double down on its “escalate to de-escalate” doctrine by adopting even riskier and more aggressive measures.
Fearing a super-capable U.S. and preoccupied with the threat of a decapitation strike, Pyongyang could be more likely to accept the downstream risks that come from adding AI-enabled processes. The first effort would be into their own nuclear command, control, and communications architecture, including early warning systems, targeting, command, control, communications, and navigation. Given North Korea’s already aggressive and risky posture, this embrace of AI can only increase the likelihood that an accidental clash could spiral into a full-on nuclear exchange. In addition, any attack on the North Korean infrastructure supporting the Korean People’s Army AI electronic warfare systems could be interpreted as a nuclear-level aggression, leading to a nuclear-level reprisal.
The efficacy of AI systems is limited by the quality of training data, sensory input, and processing power. In North Korea’s case, the quality of all three is extremely limited. This could produce false positives, which become exponentially more dangerous as humans are removed from the decision-making process. Pairing super-compressed decision timelines with automated attack protocols makes it difficult for a cool-headed human to steer the situation away from crisis. That’s doubly the case when the two states in question lack diplomatic relations, crisis communications, or confidence building measures.
Contrary to popular depictions – including Annie Jacobsen’s book “Nuclear War: A Scenario” and Kathryn Bigelow’s 2025 film “A House of Dynamite” – North Korea’s leadership understands well that launching a pre-emptive strike would be suicidal. But the alarming truth is that Pyongyang could make much more subtle and obscure posture changes that would dramatically increase the chance of accidental escalation. Facing an AGI-enabled United States, North Korea would be much more likely to hastily operationalize half-baked AI nuclear command, control, and communications, hedge with chemical and biological weapons, forward deploy additional assets, engage in gray zone attacks, and engage in aggression that blurs the line between nuclear testing and use, such as an atmospheric test near Korea or Japan that produces no casualties. They may also expand the list of red line items that trigger field commanders to independently launch a nuclear strike.
The United States faces a complex optimization problem: staying ahead of Chinese AI development while managing the nuclear deterrence instability that AGI could unleash, and the potential existential risks of AI itself. Policymakers should begin examining and counteracting these risks now, instead of scrambling in a takeoff scenario. Constraining Chinese access to advanced semiconductors is necessary but not sufficient. U.S. policymakers must also consider how their own AGI development will affect deterrence calculus in other capitals and explore voluntary restraints on capabilities that would destabilize fragile nuclear equilibria.
The next frontier of arms control should include a “human in the loop” clause such as the one featured in the 2024 agreement between the United States and China. The U.S. should lead a multilateral effort to secure buy in from all nuclear powers to commit to the same provisions and more – to wall off as much higher-function nuclear command, control, and communications from automaticity as possible. While it may seem counter-intuitive to consider that Pyongyang would accept limitations on its nuclear program, participation in such a multilateral agreement with the world’s nuclear powers might actually bestow upon it the kind of international legitimacy that Kim craves. And this sort of legitimacy is categorically different from prior offerings because it would situate North Korea among nuclear superpowers on an equitable basis, a tantalizing prospect for Kim that cannot be easily dismissed.
While some may criticize such an effort on the grounds of creating a dangerous precedent by tacitly accepting Pyongyang’s nuclear status, the time has come to stop tilting at “denuclearization” windmills in favor of achieving a material threat reduction, as one of us has argued previously. To be sure, convincing the distrustful leadership in Pyongyang to voluntarily accept limitations on its nuclear program will not be an easy sell. But the costs of inaction are so high and the alternatives so disagreeable that, in the land of lousy policy options, this is an endeavor worthy of focus, energy, and political capital.
Beijing could play a role in containing nuclear-related and asymmetric biological risks. Given the risks of powerful AI diffusing biological research capabilities, and enabling an asymmetric counter to AGI, both the U.S. and China have an interest in constraining AI’s publicly-accessible biological capabilities. The same applies to limiting North Korea’s nuclear capabilities. As during the Six Party Talks, Beijing should be recruited to support Pyongyang’s engagement and implementation.
Over time, such a framework could begin to eat away at the distrust that fuels North Korea’s paranoia and spurs its aggressive nuclear posture. If Kim Jong Un continues to reject good faith efforts, then the U.S. and its allies South Korea and Japan should invest substantially and collaboratively on missile defense architecture and other capabilities needed to address the threat and maintain deterrence. That consequence should incentivize China to act responsibly.

title: Four more mainland Chinese universities to admit Hong Kong students on DSE results from 2027
zh_title: 2027年起又有四所内地大学将凭DSE成绩录取香港学生
summary: 自2027年起，香港学生可凭DSE成绩申请入学的计划又增加了四所内地高等教育机构，使参与学校总数达到169所。 浙江财经大学。图片：浙江财经大学 中国教育部周一宣布，2027/28学年参与内地高等学校招收香港学生的院校将增至169所。机构遍布全国21个省份
content:
自2027年起，香港学生可凭DSE成绩申请入学的计划又增加了四所内地高等教育机构，使参与学校总数达到169所。 浙江财经大学。图片：浙江财经大学 中国教育部周一宣布，2027/28学年参与内地高等学校招收香港学生的院校将增至169所。机构遍布全国21个省市及内蒙古、广西壮族自治区。新加入的四所院校分别是浙江财经大学、丽水大学、广州新华大学和福耀科技大学。该计划接受香港中学文凭（DSE）考试成绩，并豁免香港学生参加中国的统一入学考试——这是一种专为香港、澳门和台湾学生设计的特殊大学入学考试，而不是众所周知的竞争激烈的国家考试（即高考）。教育局发言人表示，这些内地院校提供多元化课程，鼓励香港学生考虑接受高等教育。
发言人在一份声明中表示：“我们鼓励香港学生通过招生计划到内地升学，抓住机会了解国家最新的社会、经济和文化状况，为自己的未来发展做好规划。”档案照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。该计划还设有校长提名机制，允许中学校长提名最多八名学生。在此轨道下，申请人必须在公民身份和社会发展方面至少取得“达标”成绩，并且在三个核心科目（中文、英语和数学）中的总分至少达到八分，并且任何科目的分数不得低于二分。学生可以在12月1日至31日期间在线申请，并在明年1月10日前确认申请。 1月31日前缴纳港币460元申请费。由教育部港澳台办公室、大学生事务司和教育局联合主办的2027/28内地高等教育博览会将于12月5日至6日举行。香港一直鼓励本地学生到内地升学，同时增加大学招收非本地学生，其中不少来自内地。
自2026/27学年起，本市公立大学自资课程的非本地学生招生限额已提高至本地学生名额的50%。

【原文 English Original】
Four more mainland higher education institutions have been added to a scheme allowing Hong Kong students to seek admission based on their DSE results from 2027, bringing the total number of participating schools to 169. Zhejiang University of Finance & Economics. Photo: Zhejiang University of Finance & Economics China’s Ministry of Education announced on Monday that the number of institutions participating in the Scheme for Admission of Hong Kong Students to Mainland Higher Education Institutions will increase to 169 for the 2027/28 academic year. The institutions are located in 21 provinces or municipalities and the autonomous regions of Inner Mongolia and Guangxi Zhuang. The four newly participating institutions are Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics, Lishui University, Guangzhou Xinhua University and Fuyao University of Science and Technology. The scheme accepts the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education (DSE) exam results and exempts Hong Kong students from taking China’s joint entrance examination – a special university entrance exam designed for students from Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan as opposed to the notoriously competitive national exam, known as the Gaokao. A spokesperson for the Education Bureau (EDB) said these mainland institutions offered diverse programmes and encouraged Hong Kong students to consider them for higher education. “We encourage Hong Kong students to pursue further studies on the Chinese Mainland through the Admission Scheme and seize the opportunity to learn about the country’s latest social, economic and cultural landscape, and plan ahead for their future development,” the spokesperson said in a statement. Secondary school students in Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/ HKFP. The scheme also features a principal nomination mechanism allowing secondary school principals to nominate up to eight students. Under this track, applicants must achieve at least an “attained” grade in Citizenship and Social Development and a minimum total score of eight across the three core subjects – Chinese Language, English Language and Mathematics – with no score below two in any of those subjects. Students can apply online from December 1 to 31 and confirm their application before January 10 next year. They should pay an application fee of HK$460 by January 31. The Mainland Higher Education Expo 2027/28, jointly organised by the Office of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan Affairs and the Department of College Students Affairs of the Ministry of Education, and the EDB, will be held on December 5 and 6. Hong Kong has been encouraging local students to study in mainland China while increasing the intake of non-local students at its universities, many of whom come from the mainland. Starting from the 2026/27 academic year, the enrolment limit for non-local students in self-financing programmes at the city’s publicly funded universities has been raised to 50 per cent of local student places.

title: The Future of AI Is Not China
zh_title: 人工智能的未来不是中国
summary: 青少年科技神童内森·陈 (Nathan Chen) 是 Moonshot AI 的主要创新者，Moonshot AI 是中国几家顶级实验室之一，这在硅谷引发了人们对中国在人工智能霸主竞赛中取得进展的担忧。但上个月，陈在 X 上发帖表示，他已经离开了这家总部位于北京的公司。他现在就职于 Discovery Loop，这是一家位于帕洛阿尔托的新人工智能初创公司，拥有越来越稳定的知名人才。也许陈意识到人工智能领域最令人兴奋的进步并没有发生在中国——尽管该技术在美国的推出最近看起来比以往任何时候都更加麻烦。新电子
content:
青少年科技神童内森·陈 (Nathan Chen) 是 Moonshot AI 的主要创新者，Moonshot AI 是中国几家顶级实验室之一，这在硅谷引发了人们对中国在人工智能霸主竞赛中取得进展的担忧。但上个月，陈在 X 上发帖表示，他已经离开了这家总部位于北京的公司。他现在就职于 Discovery Loop，这是一家位于帕洛阿尔托的新人工智能初创公司，拥有越来越稳定的知名人才。也许陈意识到人工智能领域最令人兴奋的进步并没有发生在中国——尽管该技术在美国的推出最近看起来比以往任何时候都更加麻烦。新获得权力的民主党人在部分程度上由于公众对数据中心的反对而迎来了中期胜利，他们呼吁控制建设计划。英伟达（Nvidia）是一家美国芯片制造商，几乎凭借一己之力推动了人工智能的繁荣，其性丑闻，也可能是间谍丑闻，导致该公司前首席执行官黄仁勋丢掉了工作；引发美国金融市场动荡；并使整个人工智能经济陷入危机。但中国似乎仍然落后。中国人工智能公司缺乏所需的芯片——黄的倒台很可能会使这个问题变得更糟——而且它们无法筹集足够的资金来与富有的美国竞争对手竞争。
公众对这种可能会扼杀就业的技术的抵制似乎正在增长，而痴迷于安全的共产党一直看好人工智能解决中国日益严峻的经济挑战的潜力，最近似乎对人工智能可能对党的权力控制构成的威胁持谨慎态度。这种态度转变可能会进一步阻碍人工智能在中国的进步。新兴技术的支持者认为，人工智能将带来社会效益——提高经济生产力，快速推动科学进步，并增强军事能力。中国领导人宣称这项技术对于国家的持续崛起至关重要，而美国的科技高管和国家安全专家则将人工智能的追求视为一场争夺技术主导地位的生存竞赛，一场两国之间赢家通吃的竞争，将决定全球力量平衡。一些分析人士质疑人工智能的地缘政治是否完全是零和博弈，但如果人工智能的进步最终确实为最能利用这些工具的国家带来决定性的战略优势，那么中国领导人应该感到担忧。 Anthropic 定于本周进行的首次公开募股，展示了美国公司所享有的、而其中国竞争对手只能梦想的获得资本的方式。 Anthropic 预计将通过在纳斯达克首次亮相以及向包括谷歌和微软在内的投资者直接出售股票筹集超过 900 亿美元的资金。
相比之下，中国初创企业再爱科技 (Z.ai) 作为中国第一家在香港证券交易所上市的生成人工智能公司，于 1 月份筹集了 5.58 亿美元，并在随后的两次股票发行中筹集了 90 亿美元。对于付费客户来说，情况也是如此。 Anthropic 公布 2026 年上半年的收入超过 160 亿美元，而 Z.ai 的收入为 1.42 亿美元。中国企业偏爱的商业模式将很难缩小这一差距。大多数公司都将其标准模型开源，这意味着该技术可以免费使用和更新，并出售其最先进模型的使用权。但在中国拥挤的人工智能领域，对客户的激烈竞争正在压低费用。本月早些时候，中国科技巨头阿里巴巴聘请了直播主播李佳琦。

【原文 English Original】
Nathan Chen, a teenage tech prodigy, was a leading innovator at Moonshot AI, one of several top Chinese labs that have sparked fears in Silicon Valley that China is gaining ground in the race for AI supremacy. But last month, Chen posted on X that he had left the Beijing-based company. He is now at Discovery Loop, a new Palo Alto–based AI start-up with a growing stable of high-profile talent. Perhaps Chen sensed that the most exciting advances in AI were not happening in China—despite the fact that the technology’s rollout in the United States has lately looked more troubled than ever. Newly empowered Democrats, ushered to midterm victories thanks in part to public opposition to data centers, are calling to rein in construction plans. A sex scandal, possibly also a spy scandal, at Nvidia—a U.S. chipmaker that has almost single-handedly enabled the AI boom—has cost Jensen Huang, its former chief executive, his job; fomented turmoil in U.S. financial markets; and plunged the entire AI economy into crisis. But China still appears to be falling behind. Chinese AI firms are short of chips they need—a problem that Huang’s downfall might well make worse—and they can’t raise enough capital to compete with their wealthy American rivals. Public resistance to the potentially job-killing technology seems to be growing, and the security-obsessed Communist Party, which has been bullish on the potential for AI to fix China’s mounting economic challenges, has lately appeared wary of the threats it might pose to the party’s grip on power. This attitude shift could further hamper AI’s progress in the country. Proponents of the emerging technology argue that AI will bring societal benefits—boosting economic productivity, fast-tracking scientific advances, and strengthening military capabilities. China’s leaders have touted the technology as crucial to the country’s continued rise, and tech executives and national-security experts in the United States have framed the pursuit of AI as an existential race for technological dominance, a winner-takes-all competition between the two countries that will determine the global balance of power. Some analysts question whether the geopolitics of AI are so neatly zero-sum, but if advances do end up conferring a decisive strategic advantage to the country that best harnesses these tools, then China’s leaders should be worried. Anthropic’s initial public offering, scheduled for this week, demonstrates the kind of access to capital that American firms enjoy and their Chinese competitors can only dream of. Anthropic is expected to raise more than $90 billion from its Nasdaq debut and direct sale of stock to investors, including Google and Microsoft. By comparison, a Chinese start-up known as Z.ai raised $558 million as the country’s first generative-AI firm on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, in January, and an additional $9 billion in two subsequent share offerings. The story is the same when it comes to paying customers. Anthropic posted revenues of more than $16 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with Z.ai’s $142 million . The business model preferred by Chinese firms will make it hard to close this gap. Most offer their standard models open-source, which means the tech is free to use and update, and sell access to their most advanced models. But in China’s crowded AI sector, fierce competition for customers is driving down fees. Earlier this month, the Chinese tech giant Alibaba tapped Li Jiaqi, a livestreamer and beauty influencer known as the “Lipstick King,” to pitch a temporary promotion in monthly membership fees for the company’s AI productivity platform, from 28 yuan down to .01 yuan—or .0015 cents. [ Matteo Wong: A $5.7 trillion face-plant ] Chinese firms are also at a serious disadvantage in computing power. Washington has imposed export restrictions on Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China, and China’s own chipmakers have yet to make a product that matches their power. Chinese companies have tried to evade these controls by tapping cloud services and data centers outside the country and smuggling in banned Nvidia chips. But Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy will likely lead to the closure of at least some of these loopholes. Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal (no relation), was a top executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud-computing firm that has been under investigation by the U.S. federal government for illegally funneling Nvidia chips to China. Lawmakers from both parties have announced plans in recent days to add measures tightening restrictions on chip exports to the defense package currently stalled in Congress. Chinese labs have demonstrated that they are able to build competitive AI models with less money and computing power than their U.S. rivals. But the advantages that America’s AI sector has in funds, infrastructure, and chips promise to compound over time. Chinese companies appear to have responded to this resource gap by devoting their energies to building lower-cost products for a wider user base, rather than trying to make the most intelligent cutting-edge models. “I don’t actually think at any point over the past two years that Chinese companies have been trying to beat the U.S. on intelligence,” Kendra Schaefer, a partner at the research firm Trivium China who specializes in Chinese AI, told me. “It has not been part of the strategy at all, because they know they can’t win.” Chinese AI engineers have instead set their sights on where they can aggressively compete. For example, China’s massive manufacturing base would seem to grant an advantage in developing embodied AI for operating robots and other hardware. But here, too, technology from America is leading the way. Last month, Wang Xingxing, the CEO of Unitree, a top Chinese developer of humanoid robots, gushed about the capabilities of OpenAI’s newly released ChatGPT-6 Astra model for advancing the movements and actions of intelligent machines. China might also seem to have an edge over the U.S. when it comes to the speed with which individuals and companies are adopting the technology. The Chinese government has an ambitious plan to spread AI through every aspect of its economy and society by 2035, and surveys find that Chinese people are far more optimistic than Americans about AI. This has raised concerns in the U.S. that China is doing a better job of realizing gains from the new technology. But Martin Chorzempa, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics, has found that in practice, American companies are integrating AI into their operations more extensively than Chinese companies, which means they “are able to get a lot more out of it,” he told me. He added that there is “zero” evidence that AI is spreading faster and deeper in China. China’s leaders seem to have also grown warier of AI and the risks it could pose to the country’s political and economic stability. Beijing’s spy chief, Chen Yixin, recently called for greater regulation of AI to prevent China’s adversaries from using the technology to spread misinformation or to launch cyberattacks on critical Chinese infrastructure. But Chinese authorities appear just as nervous about more prosaic uses of the technology. A recent editorial in the People’s Daily , the Communist Party’s mouthpiece, criticized some popular AI-generated videos that imagined a romance between two beloved characters from classic Chinese literature as “malicious alterations that ridicule heroes.” Chinese social-media companies duly scrubbed the short films from their platforms—in keeping with a wider government ban on AI-generated content that, in the eyes of the state, distorts Chinese history and culture and threatens to manipulate public opinion. In a country where the government seeks to control the national story, even the most innocuous AI creations can seem ominously subversive and worth suppressing. Public anxiety about AI’s effect on jobs is also spreading, which may pose some obstacles on Chinese companies that hope to use the technology to increase productivity and cut costs. One of the country’s most popular chili-sauce brands, Lao Gan Ma, came under fire last month after the company’s chief quality officer credited AI with reducing product-defect rates and increasing revenues. These comments quickly circulated online, along with reports that the technology had allowed Lao Gan Ma to lay off hundreds of workers—a claim that the company has denied. Some consumers have responded by calling for a boycott of the sauce. As one commenter wrote: “Their layoff is our future.” [ Liza Lin: China has no use for AI doomerism ] Despite efforts to encourage companies to adopt the technology, China’s leaders are also clearly worried about related job losses. The government released new guidelines last month for beefing up job training and support for workers displaced by AI. These new provisions also allow regulators to weigh the potential job losses from AI-related ventures that require state approval, such as an expansion of robotaxis, suggesting that the government may intervene to prevent large-scale layoffs. AI is meant to help companies become more productive by allowing them to cut staff, yet China appears willing to sacrifice some of these benefits if it means preserving the social order. In the U.S., the fragmented regulatory landscape for AI gives companies, developers, and employers a great deal of latitude for exploiting the technology’s benefits. Perhaps the very idea that China and the United States are engaged in a high-stakes race for AI dominance misunderstands the situation. China might simply be claiming a role in AI that the country has taken in so many other industries: as a low-cost producer, offering sufficiently capable services at cheap prices that complement rather than rival the superior products sold for higher fees in the U.S. As in other industries, the demand for AI products at both the high and low end should be strong. But if China’s government continues to block American AI models from operating in the country, these seemingly symbiotic market niches won’t end up serving the Chinese people, who will be largely doomed to the exclusive use of their country’s inferior products. If the Communist Party seeks to control what Chinese AI companies get to use and how they get to use it, then the United States will enjoy a monopoly not only on superior AI but also on the freedom to make the most of it.

title: Jensen Huang could be plotting return as Nvidia CEO, report claims
zh_title: 报告称，黄仁勋可能会重新担任英伟达首席执行官
summary: 英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 因婚外情（包括与一名所谓的中国间谍）的婚外情而离开公司几天后，他可能会回到他创办的公司。在此之前，他的许多盟友联合起来支持黄，其中包括颇具影响力的 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和直言不讳的 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney)。这两人只是要求英伟达董事会重新考虑的人中的两人，希望董事会选择“把詹森带回公司”。据英国《金融时报》报道，黄现在正在讨论这种可能性。 ”黄曾机智地讨论过
content:
英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 因婚外情（包括与一名所谓的中国间谍）的婚外情而离开公司几天后，他可能会回到他创办的公司。在此之前，他的许多盟友联合起来支持黄，其中包括颇具影响力的 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和直言不讳的 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney)。这两人只是要求英伟达董事会重新考虑的人中的两人，希望董事会选择“把詹森带回公司”。据英国《金融时报》报道，黄现在正在讨论这种可能性。报道称，“据多位知情人士透露，黄已经与密友讨论了回归的可能性。”并补充说，盟友们正在组建一个由硅谷人物组成的“作战室”，试图游说他的回归。黄仁勋在发表声明证实自己的恋情后辞去英伟达职务，该声明的影响可能远远超出英伟达本身。据报道，美国情报部门认为，与黄仁勋有染的女子艾丽丝·黄（无亲属关系）是为中国国家安全部（MSS）工作的间谍。黄女士是人工智能公司 Megaspeed 的高管，该公司被指控通过一家名为 Speedmatrix 的子公司走私价值 20 亿美元的人工智能芯片到中国。自从黄仁勋承认自己通奸后，有人进一步指控他有第二次外遇，这次是与一位向他汇报的英伟达高管。
仅此一点就可能违反英伟达自己的行为准则。但对于这位前任但可能回归的首席执行官来说，与涉嫌中国间谍的事件可能是最麻烦的。现在，黄仁勋的盟友向英伟达董事会发出了一封公开信，敦促他们保留“所有选择，包括黄仁勋可能回归”。这封公开信由 Altimeter Capital 创始人 Brad Gerstner 和 Atreides Management 老板 Gavin Baker 撰写，两人均为股东。 @yunta_tsai 一份恢复 Jensen 的请愿书正在进行中，我也将于 2026 年 11 月 13 日签署。但是，Nvidia 已经开始寻找其他地方。在任命首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)临时负责后，据信该公司已与 Arm 首席执行官雷内·哈斯(Rene Haas)接洽，将其作为黄仁勋的潜在继任者。哈斯在 Nvidia 工作了大约七年，然后于 2013 年离职，但官方尚未宣布确认消息，在做出决定之前也不太可能公布。黄仁勋有可能获得美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的信任投票，因为两人迄今为止关系良好。但特朗普最近呼吁苹果前首席执行官蒂姆·库克接任英伟达。在白宫之外，黄还有其他问题需要处理。国会已传唤他就其与中国间谍嫌疑人的关系出庭，并威胁在必要时传唤他。

【原文 English Original】
Just days after he left the company under a cloud of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang might be on his way back to the company he founded. That's after a number of his allies rallied in support for Huang, including influential SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and outspoken Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. The pair are just two of those demanding that Nvidia's board has a rethink, hoping that it will choose to "Bring Jensen Back" to the company. Huang is now discussing that possibility, according to a Financial Times report . "Huang has discussed with confidantes the possibility of returning, according to multiple people familiar with the matter," the report claimed, adding that allies were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley figures to try and lobby for his return. Huang's resignation from his Nvidia post came after he released a statement confirming his affair , one which could have repercussions far beyond Nvidia itself. U.S. intelligence was reported to believe that the woman involved in an affair with Jensen Huang, Alice Huang (no relation), is a spy working for the Chinese Ministry of State Security , or MSS. Ms. Huang was an executive at Megaspeed, an AI company accused of smuggling $2 billion worth of AI chips into China via a subsidiary called Speedmatrix. Since Jensen Huang admitted to his adultery, it was further alleged that he had a second affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported to him . That alone would potentially constitute a violation of Nvidia's own code of conduct. But the affair with an alleged Chinese spy is likely to be the most troublesome for the former-but-potentially-returning CEO. Now, an open letter sent to Nvidia's board by Huang's allies has urged them to leave “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang.” The open letter was penned by Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker, both shareholders. @yunta_tsai A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too November 13, 2026 However, Nvidia has already started looking elsewhere. After placing chief financial officer Colette Kress in charge on an interim basis, it's believed the company has approached Arm chief executive Rene Haas as a potential Huang successor . Haas spent around seven years at Nvidia before leaving in 2013, but no official confirmation has been announced, nor is it likely to be until a decision is made. It's possible that Huang can expect a vote of confidence from U.S. President Donald Trump, with the pair having a good relationship to date. But Trump recently called for former Apple CEO Tim Cook to take over at Nvidia . Outside of the White House, Huang has other concerns to deal with. Congress has summoned him to appear before a Select Committee over his affair with the suspected Chinese spy, threatening to subpoena him if necessary .

title: Global solar installations face first annual decline in eight years
zh_title: 全球太阳能装机量面临八年来首次年度下降
summary: 总部位于伦敦的分析公司 GlobalData 表示，继 2025 年增长 17.5% 至创纪录水平之后，2026 年全球太阳能光伏发电增量将出现自 2018 年以来的首次下降。该公司将增长放缓归因于中国市场改革、美国政策变化和巴基斯坦经济放缓。 GlobalData电力分析师Attaurrahman Ojindaram Saibasan表示：“2026年的下降反映了一些大型市场的政策转变，而不是太阳能基本面的疲软，其中中国转向市场化电价是导致下降的主要原因。”该公司表示，预计全球累计光伏产能
content:
总部位于伦敦的分析公司 GlobalData 表示，继 2025 年增长 17.5% 至创纪录水平之后，2026 年全球太阳能光伏发电增量将出现自 2018 年以来的首次下降。该公司将增长放缓归因于中国市场改革、美国政策变化和巴基斯坦经济放缓。 GlobalData电力分析师Attaurrahman Ojindaram Saibasan表示：“2026年的下降反映了一些大型市场的政策转变，而不是太阳能基本面的疲软，其中中国转向市场化电价是导致下降的主要原因。”该公司表示，预计从2025年到2035年，全球累计光伏发电容量将以12.5%的复合年增长率增长，使太阳能在全球电力中的份额增加一倍以上。中国占 2025 年增量的一半以上，其次是美国和印度。印度的新增装机量增长了 87.2%，巴基斯坦的装机量增长了 34.3%，屋顶和离网需求使其成为第四大市场。 GlobalData 表示，中东和非洲的新增数量几乎增加了两倍，而欧洲则增长了 2.6%，北美则下降了 3.6%。该公司表示，由于白银和电池成本上涨、中国4月份的出口退税调整以及北京的“反内卷”运动推高了2026年初的价格，组件价格的长期下降已经停止。Saibasan表示，电网限制现在是增长的主要障碍，指出中国的限电、欧洲的负电价以及美国、印度和巴西的并网排队。
“电池成本下降是应对电网拥堵、限电和负电价的主要因素。太阳能+储能现在在资源丰富地区的稳定供应方面具有竞争力，使太阳能能够超越白天发电并争夺全天候供应，”他说。 “尽早将太阳能与存储和安全电网接入结合起来的开发商和投资者将最有能力抓住 2027 年的复苏机会。”该预测遵循 GlobalData 3 月份的预测，即到 2031 年全球太阳能发电容量将达到 6 TW。国际能源署光伏发电系统计划估计，2025年全球太阳能新增装机容量将达到690吉瓦，国际能源署10月预测2026年全球可再生能源新增装机容量将下降11%，这主要是因为中国太阳能部署放缓。 《全球太阳能装机量面临八年来首次年度下降》一文首先发表在光伏杂志《全球》上。

【原文 English Original】
London-based analytics firm GlobalData said annual global solar PV additions will decline in 2026 for the first time since 2018, after rising 17.5% to a record in 2025. It attributed the slowdown to market reforms in China, policy changes in the United States and a slowdown in Pakistan. “The 2026 dip reflects policy shifts in a few large markets rather than a weakening of solar’s fundamentals, with China’s move to market-based tariffs accounting for most of the decline,” said Attaurrahman Ojindaram Saibasan, a power analyst at GlobalData. The company said it expects global cumulative PV capacity to grow at a compound annual rate of 12.5% from 2025 to 2035, more than doubling solar’s share of global electricity. China accounted for more than half of 2025 additions, followed by the United States and India. India’s additions rose 87.2%, and Pakistan’s grew 34.3% as rooftop and off-grid demand made it the fourth-largest market. Additions in the Middle East and Africa nearly tripled, while Europe’s rose 2.6% and North America’s fell 3.6%, said GlobalData. The company said the long decline in module prices has stalled, as higher silver and cell costs, China’s export tax rebate adjustment in April and Beijing’s “anti-involution” campaign pushed prices up in early 2026. Saibasan said grid constraints are now the main barrier to growth, pointing to curtailment in China, negative power prices in Europe and connection queues in the United States, India and Brazil. “Falling battery costs are the main counterweight to grid congestion, curtailment, and negative power prices. Solar-plus-storage is now competitive for firm supply in high-resource regions, allowing solar to move beyond daytime generation and compete for round-the-clock supply,” he said. “Developers and investors that pair solar with storage and secure grid access early will be best placed to capture the recovery from 2027.” The forecast follows GlobalData’s March projection that global solar capacity will reach 6 TW by 2031 . The International Energy Agency’s Photovoltaic Power Systems Programme has estimated that global solar additions hit 690 GW in 2025 , and in October the International Energy Agency forecast an 11% fall in global renewable capacity additions in 2026, mainly because of slower solar deployment in China. The post Global solar installations face first annual decline in eight years appeared first on pv magazine Global .

title: AI model detects small fires, smoke in PV plants
zh_title: AI模型检测光伏电站中的小火、烟雾
summary: 中国国有公用事业公司中国华能集团的一个研究团队开发了一种新的深度学习框架，用于光伏电站的实时火灾和烟雾检测。该系统被称为PVFire-YOLO，旨在检测小火焰和烟雾羽流，同时减少光伏组件表面反射的阳光引起的误报。 “对于光伏检测这一特定领域，深度学习研究集中在三个问题：电致发光（EL）裂纹检测、红外（IR）热点定位以及面板级可见光异常检测（例如表面缺陷和污垢）
content:
中国国有公用事业公司中国华能集团的一个研究团队开发了一种新的深度学习框架，用于光伏电站的实时火灾和烟雾检测。该系统被称为PVFire-YOLO，旨在检测小火焰和烟雾羽流，同时减少光伏组件表面反射的阳光引起的误报。研究人员表示：“对于光伏检测的特定领域，深度学习研究集中在三个问题：电致发光（EL）裂纹检测、红外（IR）热点定位以及面板级可见光异常检测（例如表面缺陷和污染）。” “相比之下，光伏环境中的火灾探测几乎没有得到专门的处理。”研究人员表示，他们编制了第一个专为光伏环境设计的带注释的火焰和烟雾数据集。他们补充说：“新的带注释的语料库 PV-Fire 将来自运行中的公用事业规模工厂的监视和无人机图像与在真实光伏模块中上演的受控户外燃烧相结合。”该方法基于 YOLOv12 实时目标检测模型，并结合了三个附加组件来改进光伏环境中的火灾检测。补丁感知注意力块增强了微弱的火焰和烟雾特征，而收集和分发机制则结合了四个特征级别的信息。自适应融合头添加了高分辨率检测分支来识别小目标。
研究人员组装了 PV-Fire 数据集，其中包含 5,824 张图像以及 9,107 个带注释的火焰和烟雾对象。该数据集结合了监视和无人机图像、受控户外燃烧和合成图像。他们分配了 4,070 张图像用于训练，870 张用于验证，884 张用于测试。他们还将三个子集的场景分开，并将合成图像限制在训练集中。该团队使用 PV-Fire 数据集将 PVFire-YOLO 与 14 个现有检测模型进行了比较，包括 Faster R-CNN、基于 Transformer 的模型和几个 YOLO 变体。他们还使用公开的 D-Fire 数据集将其与 13 个替代模型进行了基准测试。这些测试评估了检测精度、小目标性能、反射引起的误报、跨数据集泛化以及桌面和嵌入式硬件上的处理速度。结果是三次训练的平均值。 PVFire-YOLO 在 PV-Fire 数据集上的交集阈值为 0.5 (mAP@50) 时实现了 87.4% 的平均精度。当测试仅限于运行光伏电站的镜头时，该数字为 85.0%，而在 D-Fire 数据集上，该数字为 84.4%。与基线YOLOv12模型相比，该方法小目标平均精度提高了5.2个百分点。它还将与反射相关的误报率降低至 3.1%，同时检测到更高比例的实际火焰和烟雾目标。
研究人员总结道：“该模型在 RTX 3090 桌面显卡上以 79 帧/秒的速度运行，在 Jetson Orin Nano 紧凑型人工智能计算机上以 21 帧/秒的速度运行，满足分布式植物监测中实时边缘部署的延迟预算。未来的工作将把语料库扩展到不同气候下的植物，结合时间过滤来抑制孤立的误报，并将可见光检测与红外热成像融合，以增强不利照明下的鲁棒性。”研究结果发表在“光伏电站实时小目标火灾检测”中

【原文 English Original】
A research team from Chinese state-owned utility China Huaneng Group has developed a new deep-learning framework for real-time fire and smoke detection in PV power plants. Dubbed PVFire-YOLO, the system is designed to detect small flames and smoke plumes while reducing false alarms caused by sunlight reflected from PV module surfaces. “For the specific domain of PV inspection, deep-learning research has concentrated on three problems: electroluminescence (EL) crack detection, infrared (IR) hot-spot localization, and panel-level visible-light anomaly detection such as surface defects and soiling,” the researchers said. “Fire detection in PV environments has, by contrast, received almost no dedicated treatment.” The researchers said they compiled the first annotated flame-and-smoke dataset specifically designed for PV environments. “The new annotated corpus, PV-Fire, combines surveillance and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery from operating utility-scale plants with controlled outdoor burns staged among real PV modules,” they added. The proposed method is based on the YOLOv12 real-time object detection model and incorporates three additional components to improve fire detection in PV environments. A patch-aware attention block enhances weak flame and smoke features, while a gather-and-distribute mechanism combines information across four feature levels. An adaptive fusion head adds a high-resolution detection branch to identify small targets. The researchers assembled the PV-Fire dataset, comprising 5,824 images with 9,107 annotated flame and smoke objects. The dataset combines surveillance and drone imagery, controlled outdoor burns, and synthetic images. They allocated 4,070 images for training, 870 for validation, and 884 for testing. They also separated scenes across the three subsets and restricted synthetic images to the training set. The team compared PVFire-YOLO with 14 existing detection models using the PV-Fire dataset, including Faster R-CNN, transformer-based models, and several YOLO variants. They also benchmarked it against 13 alternative models using the publicly available D-Fire dataset. The tests assessed detection accuracy, small-target performance, false alarms caused by reflections, cross-dataset generalization, and processing speed on desktop and embedded hardware. The results were averaged across three training runs. PVFire-YOLO achieved a mean average precision of 87.4% at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.5 (mAP@50) on the PV-Fire dataset. The figure was 85.0% when testing was restricted to footage from operating PV plants and 84.4% on the D-Fire dataset. Compared with the baseline YOLOv12 model, the proposed method improved small-target average precision by 5.2 percentage points. It also reduced the reflection-related false-positive rate to 3.1% while detecting a higher proportion of actual flame and smoke targets. “Running at 79 frames/s on an RTX 3090 desktop graphics card and 21 frames/s on a Jetson Orin Nano compact AI computer, the model meets the latency budget for real-time edge deployment in distributed plant monitoring,” the researchers concluded. “Future work will extend the corpus to plants in diverse climates, incorporate temporal filtering to suppress isolated false positives, and fuse visible light detection with infrared thermal imaging to enhance robustness under adverse illumination.” The findings are presented in the study “ Real time small target fire detection in photovoltaic plants using attention enhanced multiscale fusion ,” published in Scientific Reports . The post AI model detects small fires, smoke in PV plants appeared first on pv magazine Global .

Fandango 表示黑客从结帐页面窃取了支付卡详细信息
Fandango 表示黑客从结帐页面窃取了支付卡详细信息
Fandango 表示黑客从结帐页面窃取了支付卡详细信息
门票销售商 Fandango Media 正在向客户通报一次数据泄露事件，该事件导致其结账页面上输入的支付卡详细信息遭到泄露。
该公司表示，这些细节是在10月8日至11日期间曝光的，这影响了通过其官方网站购买的客户。
注入 Fandango 结账页面的银行卡窃取器代码拦截了下订单时输入的支付卡详细信息，并将数据发送给黑客。
Fandango Media 是美国主要的在线电影票务平台。该公司通过其网站和应用程序向 31,000 个美国电影院出售门票，其中包括 AMC、Regal 和 Cinemark。
该公司还运营着颇受欢迎的电影评论网站烂番茄。
“我们的调查发现，有证据表明未经授权的一方可以访问与 2026 年 10 月 8 日至 11 日期间我们结帐页面上某些交易相关的支付卡信息，”给客户的通知中写道。
“Fandango 于 2026 年 10 月 30 日确定，您的信息可能会在此事件中受到影响。”
该公司表示以下数据类型可能已被暴露：
Fandango 表示，该事件并未泄露姓名、政府颁发的身份信息、社会安全号码 (SSN) 或任何其他帐户信息。
然而，事件中泄露的信息可能会被用于在网上商店进行未经授权的购买。
为了降低受影响客户的风险，Fandango 提供两年免费 IDX 信用和暗网监控以及身份盗窃恢复服务，注册截止日期为 2027 年 2 月 13 日。
Fandango 表示，目前已在其结帐页面上修复了该问题，并与外部网络安全专家进行了调查，目前尚未发现任何利用被盗数据的欺诈案件。
该公司尚未透露受影响客户的数量。 BleepingComputer 已联系 Fandango 了解更多信息，我们将在收到他们的回复后更新这篇文章。
在曝光期间从 Fandango 购买电影票的用户应密切监控其报表和账户活动，并向发卡机构报告任何未经授权的购买行为。
保护支付卡详细信息的一种方法是在网上购物时使用一次性虚拟卡。

Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
Ticket seller Fandango Media is notifying customers about a data breach that exposed payment card details entered on its checkout pages.
The company says the details were exposed between October 8 and 11, and it impacts customers who made purchases through its official website.
Card skimmer code injected into Fandango’s checkout page intercepted payment card details entered when placing orders, sending the data to hackers.
Fandango Media is a major U.S. online movie ticketing platform. It sells tickets through its website and app for 31,000 U.S. cinema screens, including at AMC, Regal, and Cinemark.
The company also operates the popular movie review website Rotten Tomatoes.
“Our investigation identified evidence that an unauthorized party could access payment card information associated with certain transactions on our checkout page from October 8-11, 2026,” reads the notification to customers.
“Fandango determined on October 30, 2026 that your information may have been impacted in this incident.”
The company says the following data types may have been exposed:
Fandango says the incident did not expose names, government-issued identity information, Social Security Numbers (SSNs), or any other account information.
However, the information compromised in the incident could be used for unauthorized purchases on online stores.
To reduce the risk to affected customers, Fandango is offering two years of free IDX credit and dark web monitoring, as well as identity theft recovery services, with an enrollment deadline of February 13, 2027.
Fandango says it has now fixed the issue on its checkout page, investigated with outside cybersecurity specialists, and is currently unaware of any cases of fraud leveraging the stolen data.
The company has not shared the number of affected customers. BleepingComputer has contacted Fandango to learn more, and we will update this post with their response once received.
Users who bought movie tickets from Fandango during the exposure window should monitor their statements and account activity closely, and report any unauthorized purchases to their card issuer.
One way to protect payment card details is to use one-time virtual cards when making online purchases.

香港旅行社警告客户注意第三方供应商的数据泄露中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 17 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港旅行社警告客户注意第三方供应商的数据泄露
香港旅行社 EGL Tours 表示，一家第三方技术供应商于 11 月 13 日遭遇未经授权的网络访问，可能会泄露客户姓名、联系方式、身份证件和旅行证件数据。该公司已向警方和隐私专员报告了这一事件。没有信用卡数据
香港旅行社东瀛旅游（EGL Tours）警告客户，在第三方技术服务供应商发生安全事件后，他们的个人数据可能已被泄露。该公司于11月16日表示，供应商于11月13日通知其系统遭到未经授权的网络访问，可能涉及客户姓名、联系方式、身份证号码和旅行证件信息。
东瀛旅游表示，已向警方报告此事，并向个人数据隐私专员办公室立案。该公司强调，其核心旅游预订系统和日常业务运营没有受到影响，所有已确认的旅游套餐、航班和酒店预订均保持正常。它还表示，调查证实，由于该公司使用独立的银行支付系统，因此没有涉及信用卡或支付数据，并且目前没有证据表明暴露的数据被不当使用。
香港信息科技商会名誉会长方国强表示，东瀛旅游事件的关键问题是客户数据通过第三方供应商的后端管理系统被未经授权访问，而不是公司自己的网站被直接入侵。他警告说，暴露的数据组合足以让犯罪分子进行有针对性的诈骗，例如冒充旅行社告知客户行程变更或要求额外付款，并表示风险不容低估。
方建议企业主动通知可能受影响的客户，明确说明如何避免欺诈，并要求供应商披露入侵原因以及堵塞漏洞的措施。他表示，从长远来看，企业应该审查所有第三方合作伙伴的安全要求，并尽量减少不必要的个人数据的存储，而不是仅在每次事件发生后才采取补救措施。

Hong Kong travel agency warns clients of data breach via third-party supplier | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong travel agency warns clients of data breach via third-party supplier
Hong Kong travel agency EGL Tours says a third-party tech supplier suffered unauthorised network access on 13 November, potentially exposing client names, contact details, ID and travel document data. The firm has reported the incident to police and the privacy commissioner. No credit card data was
Hong Kong travel agency EGL Tours has warned clients that their personal data may have been exposed following a security incident at a third-party technology service supplier. The company said on 16 November that it was notified by the supplier on 13 November of unauthorised network access to its systems, potentially involving client names, contact details, identity card numbers and travel document information.
EGL Tours said it has reported the matter to the police and filed a case with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data. The company stressed that its core travel booking system and daily business operations were not affected, and that all confirmed tour packages, flight and hotel bookings remain normal. It also said an investigation confirmed that no credit card or payment data were involved, as the company uses a separate bank payment system, and that there is currently no evidence that the exposed data have been improperly used.
Charles Fang, honorary president of the Hong Kong Information Technology商会, said the key issue in the EGL Tours incident is that client data were accessed without authorisation through the third-party supplier's backend management system, rather than the company's own website being directly breached. He warned that the combination of data exposed is sufficient for criminals to carry out targeted scams, such as impersonating the travel agency to inform clients of itinerary changes or request additional payments, and said the risk should not be underestimated.
Fang advised companies to proactively notify potentially affected clients, clearly explain how to avoid fraud, and demand that suppliers disclose the cause of the intrusion and the measures taken to plug vulnerabilities. In the longer term, he said, firms should review security requirements for all third-party partnerships and minimise the storage of unnecessary personal data, rather than only taking remedial action after each incident.

香港电影亮相波兰五味亚洲电影节 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 17 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港电影亮相波兰五味亚洲电影节
由香港政府文化体育及旅游局支持的十部香港电影在波兰五味亚洲电影节展映。该电影节展出了导演兼制片人徐克的八部经典作品回顾展，以及两部近期作品。官员宣传香港
根据2026年11月16日的政府声明，十部香港电影在波兰五味亚洲电影节展映，获香港政府文化体育及旅游局透过创意产业发展办公室及电影发展基金支持。
节目内容包括两部近期上映的电影《虎独步》和《世外》，以及著名导演兼制片人徐克的八部经典作品回顾展。策划这次回顾展是为了突显他对香港电影的持久影响。
11 月 12 日，香港驻柏林经济贸易办事处处长黄文忠在徐克制作的《倩女幽魂》开幕片中致辞时强调了香港电影的多样性。他说：“从动作武打片、喜剧、剧情片到具有社会意识的电影，香港电影人不断突破创意界限，体现香港精神。” “我邀请电影和创作人才来香港共同创作优质作品。”
放映结束后，经济贸易办公室举办招待会，约200名工商界和文化界嘉宾出席。黄先生借此机会介绍香港的最新发展，包括行政长官《2026年施政报告》提出设立海外电影制作支援小组。该单元将为内地及海外影视制作团队来港拍摄提供一站式服务，吸引更多优质作品，宣传香港。
访问期间，黄先生亦与当地商会、记者及初创组织会面，宣传香港独特优势，探讨近期发展及合作机遇。
香港驻柏林经济贸易办事处是香港特别行政区政府驻德国、奥地利、捷克、匈牙利、波兰、斯洛伐克、斯洛文尼亚和瑞士的官方代表，处理商业关系及其他贸易事宜。

Hong Kong films showcased at Poland's Five Flavours Asian Film Festival | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong films showcased at Poland's Five Flavours Asian Film Festival
Ten Hong Kong films were screened at Poland's Five Flavours Asian Film Festival, supported by the Hong Kong government's Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau. The festival featured a retrospective of eight classics by director-producer Tsui Hark, alongside two recent works. Officials promoted Hong Kon
Ten Hong Kong films were screened at Poland's Five Flavours Asian Film Festival, supported by the Hong Kong government's Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau through the Creative Industries Development Office and the Film Development Fund, according to a government statement on 16 November 2026.
The programme included two recent films, Hu Du Bu and Shi Wai, as well as a retrospective of eight classic works by renowned director and producer Tsui Hark. The retrospective was curated to highlight his enduring influence on Hong Kong cinema.
Speaking at the opening film, A Chinese Ghost Story, produced by Tsui Hark, on 12 November, Director of the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Berlin, Wong Man-chung, emphasised the diversity of Hong Kong cinema. 'From action martial arts films, comedies, dramas to socially conscious films, Hong Kong filmmakers constantly push creative boundaries and embody the Hong Kong spirit,' he said. 'I invite film and creative talent to come to Hong Kong to create quality works together.'
Following the screening, the Economic and Trade Office hosted a reception attended by about 200 guests from the business and cultural sectors. Wong took the opportunity to present Hong Kong's latest developments, including a proposal from the Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address to set up an overseas film production support unit. This unit would provide one-stop services for mainland Chinese and overseas film and television production teams filming in Hong Kong, aiming to attract more high-quality productions and promote the city.
During his visit, Wong also met local chambers of commerce, journalists and start-up organisations to promote Hong Kong's unique advantages and discuss recent developments and cooperation opportunities.
The Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Berlin is the official representative of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government in Germany, Austria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia and Switzerland for commercial relations and other trade matters.

content:
香港警察被指控不当处理血液样本等待判决中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 17 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港警察被控不当处理血液样本等待判决
一名 25 岁的香港警官被指控将酒后驾驶嫌疑人的血样存放在自家冰箱中，而不是将其送去检测，他将于明年 3 月得知自己的命运。该官员面临公职行为不当和意图妨碍司法公正的指控
一名 25 岁的香港警官被指控将酒后驾驶嫌疑人的血样保存在家用冰箱中，而不是将其送去进行法医检测，该警官将于明年 3 月在区域法院的审判结案后得知自己的命运。
这名警官名叫 Ching Long，面临公职行为不当的指控，以及意图妨碍司法公正的另一项指控。双方均向副区域法院法官梁家琪提出最后陈词，梁家琪将判决押后至 3 月 2 日。
Ching 的代表律师辩称，该警官将小瓶带回家可能是因为粗心和真正的误解，而不是犯罪意图。法庭获悉，程当时缺乏刑事调查经验，难以适应繁重的工作量，而且还患有严重疾病。辩方强调，程已通知他的上级有关将样本带回家的事情，并且没有受到谴责。此外，律师指出，Ching 将血液妥善保存在冰箱中，而不是将其丢弃，这使得样本在事件曝光时仍可用于测试。辩方敦促法院将此事件视为严重判断失误，而不是构成刑事责任的行为。
控方回应称，没有证据支持程误会上级命令的说法。检察官还反驳了声称显示程的调查部门内证据存储混乱的辩方照片，并指出控方证人对这一描述提出异议，并且没有任何证据证明所描绘的物品是官方证物。针对意图问题，检方辩称，法律并不要求政府证明被告的具体动机。虽然检察官没有详细说明程与女嫌疑人之间的关系是如何开始或运作的，但他们坚称两人关系密切，并指出在警官的手机上发现了该女子的亲密照片。
辩方对检方对 Ching 和这名女子之间关系的描述不断变化提出质疑。辩护律师辩称，检方此前曾指控 Ching 勒索和胁迫该女子，这种动态与亲密伙伴关系根本不相容，并质疑样本是否涉嫌出于感情而被隐瞒或被用作筹码。 Ching最初被指控向该女子索要30万港元，并威胁她发生性行为，导致初步指控她犯有敲诈勒索和通过威胁促成非法性行为的罪名。检方随后在选择不提供任何证据后撤销了这两项指控，仅维持了有关血液处理不当的指控。

Hong Kong police officer accused of mishandling blood sample awaits verdict | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong police officer accused of mishandling blood sample awaits verdict
A 25-year-old Hong Kong police officer accused of keeping a drink-driving suspect's blood sample in his home refrigerator instead of delivering it for testing will learn his fate in March next year. The officer faces charges of misconduct in public office and intending to pervert the course of justi
A 25-year-old Hong Kong police officer accused of keeping a drink-driving suspect's blood sample in his domestic refrigerator instead of delivering it for forensic testing will learn his fate in March next year, following the conclusion of closing submissions in his trial at the District Court.
The officer, Ching Long, faces a charge of misconduct in public office and an alternative charge of intending to pervert the course of justice. Both sides presented their final arguments before Deputy District Judge Leung Ka-kei, who adjourned the verdict to 2 March.
Counsel representing Ching argued that the officer may have taken the vial home because of carelessness and a genuine misunderstanding rather than criminal intent. The court heard that Ching was inexperienced in criminal investigations at the time, struggling to adapt to a demanding workload, and coping with serious illness. The defence emphasised that Ching had informed his superior about bringing the specimen home and was not reprimanded. Furthermore, counsel noted that Ching properly preserved the blood in his refrigerator rather than discarding it, which allowed the sample to remain viable for testing when the matter came to light. The defence urged the court to treat the incident as a grave lapse in judgment rather than conduct warranting criminal liability.
In response, the prosecution asserted that there was no evidentiary foundation to support the claim that Ching had misunderstood orders from his superiors. Prosecutors also pushed back against defence photographs purporting to show disorganised evidence storage within Ching's investigative unit, noting that prosecution witnesses disputed this characterisation and that nothing proved the items depicted were official exhibits. Addressing the issue of intent, the prosecution argued that the law does not require the government to prove the defendant's specific motive. While prosecutors did not detail how the relationship between Ching and the female suspect began or functioned, they maintained that the two shared an intimate relationship, pointing to intimate photographs of the woman found on the officer's mobile phone.
The defence challenged the prosecution's shifting characterisation of the relationship between Ching and the woman, identified only as X. Defence counsel argued that prosecutors had previously accused Ching of blackmailing and coercing the woman, dynamics fundamentally incompatible with an intimate partnership, and questioned whether the sample was allegedly concealed out of affection or used as leverage. Ching was originally accused of demanding HK$300,000 from the woman and threatening her into sexual acts, leading to initial counts of blackmail and procuring unlawful sexual acts by threats. The prosecution subsequently dropped those two charges after electing to offer no evidence on them, maintaining only the allegations concerning the mishandling of the blood sample collected between late May and mid-July two years ago.

星期二, 17 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港迪士尼乐园宣布圣诞活动至 1 月 3 日
香港迪士尼乐园将于周二至 2027 年 1 月 3 日举行圣诞节庆祝活动，包括无人机表演、降雪效果和巨型圣诞树灯光秀。公园还宣布将于 2027 年 1 月至 3 月在《冰雪奇缘》主题区举办冬季冰雪节。
香港迪士尼乐园度假区宣布从星期二至 2027 年 1 月 3 日期间将举办一系列圣诞及新年活动。庆祝活动包括每日下午 6 时 20 分为美国大街上的巨型圣诞树举行亮灯仪式，并伴有节日无人机表演和降雪效果。
该公园将继续其夜间烟花表演，并在城堡上方举行额外的无人机表演，这意味着每天晚上将举行两场无人机表演。周二下午，举行了一场发布会，韩国女团成员张元英与迪士尼人物一起点亮了大街上的巨大圣诞树，吸引了许多客人拍照。
从本周末到十二月初，香港迪士尼乐园将举办圣诞音乐会，由当地钢琴家和儿童合唱团表演。除夕夜，将举行倒计时派对，DJ 播放经典迪士尼歌曲，迪士尼人物登场，无人机、烟花和倒计时投影照亮美国大街。
该度假村还宣布，冰冻世界地区将于2027年1月至3月举办冬季冰雪节，并以新的戏剧表演为特色。

Hong Kong Disneyland announces Christmas events until 3 January | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong Disneyland announces Christmas events until 3 January
Hong Kong Disneyland will hold Christmas celebrations from Tuesday until 3 January 2027, featuring drone shows, snowfall effects, and a giant tree lighting. The park also announced a Winter Snow Festival in the Frozen-themed area from January to March 2027.
Hong Kong Disneyland Resort has announced a series of Christmas and New Year events running from Tuesday until 3 January 2027. The celebrations include a daily lighting ceremony at 6:20pm for the giant Christmas tree on Main Street, U.S.A., accompanied by a festive drone show and snowfall effects.
The park will continue its nightly fireworks display with an additional drone show above the castle, meaning two drone performances will take place each evening. On Tuesday afternoon, a launch event was held featuring South Korean girl group member Jang Wonyoung alongside Disney characters, who lit the large Christmas tree on Main Street, drawing many guests to take photos.
From this weekend until early December, Hong Kong Disneyland will host Christmas concerts featuring a local pianist and a children's choir. On New Year's Eve, a countdown party will be held with a DJ playing classic Disney songs, appearances by Disney characters, and a display of drones, fireworks and countdown projections illuminating Main Street, U.S.A.
The resort also announced that the World of Frozen area will host a Winter Snow Festival from January to March 2027, featuring a new theatre show.

第六届香港电影节重返迪拜 携六部电影亮相
The Hong Kong Film Festival in Dubai opened on 6 November with a reception hosted by the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office.六部电影突出了动作电影的传统和新的创意人才，其中包括户外放映成龙《警察故事》的 4K 修复版。
2026 年 11 月 16 日 21:02 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 16 日 21:18 · 阅读时间 3 分钟
香港电影节第六度重返迪拜，于11月6日开幕，并由香港驻迪拜经济贸易办事处（经贸办）举办酒会。三位香港演员——黄德斌、张文杰和戴钰琪——前往迪拜参加活动，活动进行了一系列放映。
香港驻迪拜办事处驻迪拜专员陈尚文致开幕词时表示，每年一度的文化节已进入第六个年头，反映了驻迪拜办事处持续致力促进香港与中东文化交流。他指出，地区观众对香港电影的兴趣稳步增长。 “迪拜是一座汇聚多元文化的国际大都市，是中东地区重要的文化中心。”陈说。 “区内创意产业近年蓬勃发展，香港电影也长期受到迪拜不同文化背景观众的喜爱，展现香港作品的跨境魅力。”
今年的节目重点关注香港动作电影的吸引力和遗产，包括两部来自不同时代的动作大片，展示该类型从 1980 年代黄金时代到现在的演变。开场影片《武士黄昏之寨城》是一部广受好评的当代动作史诗片，以现代动作美学和香港怀旧情怀再现了20世纪80年代九龙寨城的面貌。电影节首次在Alserkal Avenue星空下举行户外放映，呈现成龙1985年经典电影《警察故事》的4K修复版。两部影片均获得观众好评； 《勇士暮光之城》大受欢迎，加映场次，《警察故事》4K修复版户外放映全部售空。
除了经典和当代动作片外，该阵容还包括多部展示新一代香港创作者作品的电影。其中包括本地动画里程碑作品《彼岸世界》、首次导演林乐仙的长片处女作《我被杀的那一天》、黑色喜剧《部门的诞生》以及都市爱情片《主厨发制》，为影迷呈现多元化的香港电影图景。
三位访问迪拜的香港演员代表不同世代。老演员黄德斌和动作明星张文杰在《武士黄昏之寨》中表演了令人印象深刻的动作场面，而年轻演员戴雨琪则在《部门的诞生》中出演。他们的出现象征着香港电影火炬的传递。除了参加首映晚会外，他们还参加了多次映后问答环节，与热情的观众进行了互动。主演第四部《警察故事》的女演员吴恭如也到场支持露天放映。

Hong Kong Film Festival returns to Dubai for sixth edition with six movies
The Hong Kong Film Festival in Dubai opened on 6 November with a reception hosted by the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office. Six films highlight action cinema heritage and new creative talent, with screenings including an outdoor showing of the 4K restoration of Jackie Chan’s “Police Story”.
16 Nov 2026 at 21:02 HKT · updated 16 Nov, 21:18 · 3 min read
The Hong Kong Film Festival has returned to Dubai for the sixth time, opening on 6 November with a reception hosted by the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (HKETO) in Dubai. Three Hong Kong actors – Wong Tak Bun, Zhang Wenjie and Dai Yuqi – travelled to Dubai for the event, which runs a series of screenings.
In his opening remarks, HKETO Dubai Commissioner Chen Shangwen said the annual festival, now in its sixth year, reflects the office’s sustained efforts to promote cultural exchange between Hong Kong and the Middle East. He noted that interest in Hong Kong films among regional audiences has grown steadily. “Dubai is an international metropolis that brings together diverse cultures and is an important cultural hub in the Middle East,” Chen said. “The creative industries in the region have been flourishing in recent years, and Hong Kong films have long been popular among audiences from different cultural backgrounds in Dubai, demonstrating the cross-border appeal of Hong Kong works.”
This year’s programme focuses on the appeal and legacy of Hong Kong action cinema, featuring two action blockbusters from different eras that showcase the evolution of the genre from its 1980s golden age to the present. The opening film, “Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In”, a critically acclaimed contemporary action epic, recreates the look of the Kowloon Walled City in the 1980s with modern action aesthetics and Hong Kong nostalgia. For the first time, the festival held an outdoor screening at Alserkal Avenue under the stars, presenting the 4K restoration of Jackie Chan’s 1985 classic “Police Story”. Both films were well received by audiences; “Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In” was so popular that an additional screening was added, and the outdoor showing of “Police Story” 4K restoration was sold out.
Beyond classic and contemporary action, the line-up includes several films showcasing the work of a new generation of Hong Kong creators. These include the local animation milestone “The World Beyond”, first-time director Lam Lok Sin’s feature debut “The Day I Was Killed”, the black comedy “Birth of a Department”, and the urban romance “Omakase”, presenting a diverse picture of Hong Kong cinema to film fans.
The three Hong Kong actors visiting Dubai represent different generations. Veteran actor Wong Tak Bun and action star Zhang Wenjie, both of whom performed impressive action sequences in “Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In”, were joined by Dai Yuqi, a younger actor who stars in “Birth of a Department”. Their presence embodied the passing of the torch in Hong Kong cinema. Besides attending the opening-night reception, they took part in several post-screening Q&A sessions, engaging with enthusiastic audiences. Actress Christine Ng, who starred in the fourth “Police Story” film, also attended the outdoor screening in support.
HKETO Dubai said it will continue working with partners to promote Hong Kong’s creative and cultural industries in the UAE and the wider Middle East, fostering people-to-people ties and exploring business opportunities.

香港暂停从印度、英国和日本部分地区进口家禽中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 17 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港暂停从印度、英国和日本部分地区进口家禽
香港暂停从印度、英国和日本疫区进口家禽。此次暂停涉及每个国家的特定地区，没有从印度进口新鲜家禽，但来自英国和日本的大量贸易量受到影响。
因应禽流感疫情的报道，香港特别行政区政府于11月16日宣布暂停从印度、英国和日本指定地区进口禽肉及禽类产品。
在印度，暂停适用于安得拉邦的阿纳纳塔普尔地区。在英国，受影响的地区包括诺福克郡的金斯林和西诺福克区、东约克郡的东约克郡区、兰开夏郡的怀尔区以及附近的兰开斯特、法尔德和普雷斯顿区。在日本，暂停覆盖千叶县。
食物安全中心发言人表示，香港现时只有印度禽蛋的进口机制，并没有禽肉的进口机制。据政府统计，今年前9个月没有从印度进口禽蛋。同期，香港从英国进口约680公吨冰鲜及冷冻禽肉及约22万枚禽蛋，以及从日本进口约1,030公吨冷冻禽肉及约24,994万枚禽蛋。
发言人表示：“中心已联络印度、英国及日本当局，并会继续密切留意世界动物卫生组织及有关当局有关禽流感疫情的消息，并会根据情况发展采取适当行动。”

Hong Kong suspends poultry imports from parts of India, UK and Japan | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong suspends poultry imports from parts of India, UK and Japan
Hong Kong suspends poultry imports from disease-affected areas in India, the UK and Japan. The suspension covers specific regions in each country, with no fresh poultry imports from India and significant trade volumes from the UK and Japan affected.
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government announced on 16 November the suspension of imports of poultry meat and poultry products from specified areas in India, the United Kingdom and Japan, following reports of avian influenza outbreaks.
In India, the suspension applies to the Anantapur district in the state of Andhra Pradesh. In the UK, affected areas include King's Lynn & West Norfolk district in Norfolk, the East Yorkshire district in East Yorkshire, and the Wyre district in Lancashire along with the nearby Lancaster, Fylde and Preston districts. In Japan, the suspension covers Chiba Prefecture.
A spokesperson for the Centre for Food Safety noted that Hong Kong currently has only an import mechanism for poultry eggs from India, not for poultry meat. According to government statistics, no poultry eggs were imported from India in the first nine months of this year. During the same period, Hong Kong imported about 680 metric tonnes of chilled and frozen poultry meat and about 220,000 poultry eggs from the UK, and about 1,030 metric tonnes of frozen poultry meat and about 249.94 million poultry eggs from Japan.
The spokesperson said: “The Centre has contacted the authorities in India, the United Kingdom and Japan, and will continue to closely monitor information from the World Organisation for Animal Health and relevant authorities on avian influenza outbreaks, and will take appropriate action based on the development of the situation.”

盛智曼 (Allan Zeman) 将 APEC 峰会视为乌克兰人工智能突破的机会中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 17 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
盛智曼 (Allan Zeman) 将 APEC 峰会视为人工智能和乌克兰突破的机会
盛智文表示，深圳亚太经合组织峰会为香港与深圳的合作提供了机会，并在人工智能治理和乌克兰战争方面取得重大进展。他强调了友好城市安排以及香港在接待代表方面的作用。
兰桂坊集团主席盛智文表示，即将在深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）领导人非正式会议为香港与其北方邻国深化合作提供了绝佳机会，同时为人工智能监管和乌克兰冲突方面潜在的历史性突破提供了平台。
这位资深商界领袖在接受采访时指出，继早前在香港举行的亚太经合组织财长会议之后，双城安排为香港提供了显着的优势。他预计，众多前往深圳峰会的国际企业高管会选择途经香港或在香港停留。泽曼还透露，香港将于11月20日举办2026年亚太经合组织下一代青年企业家峰会，他将担任主讲嘉宾。他补充说，兰桂坊娱乐区正在准备欢迎代表们在整个活动期间参加晚宴和社交聚会。
泽曼表示，香港和深圳是兄弟城市，双方优势互补，能够有效推动内地企业走向国际舞台，加速粤港澳大湾区建设世界级经济区。他强调了深圳的科技活力和人工智能能力，并指出该市众多优质内地企业正在积极寻求国际扩张。反过来，香港提供了一座成熟的、全球值得信赖的桥梁，其基础是普通法法律体系、不受限制的资本流动和国际金融市场。
泽曼在反思深圳的快速现代化时表示，全球视野已经东移，西方世界部分地区现在面临着日益恶化的状况，与亚洲的进步形成鲜明对比。
泽曼曾出席过七次亚太经合组织会议，他强调，在地缘政治紧张局势不稳定的情况下，高层领导人之间的面对面外交仍然不可或缺。他承认之前的峰会通常以一般性讨论而非具有约束力的决议结束，但他表示，即将举行的会议可以在涉及中国、美国和俄罗斯领导人的两个重大国际问题上取得有意义的进展。第一个潜在的突破涉及人工智能。随着全世界对先进自动化系统不受控制的发展和生存风险的担忧日益加剧，泽曼预计，主要大国可能会举行磋商，旨在建立类似于《不扩散核武器条约》的全球安全护栏和治理标准。
第二个潜在进展领域集中在旷日持久的俄罗斯-乌克兰战争上。泽曼指出，国家元首之间的三方讨论可以探讨停火的途径，以停止人员伤亡并缓解更广泛的人道主义危机。

Allan Zeman sees APEC summit as chance for AI, Ukraine breakthroughs | China Labour Bulletin Board
Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Allan Zeman sees APEC summit as chance for AI, Ukraine breakthroughs
Allan Zeman says the APEC summit in Shenzhen offers a chance for Hong Kong-Shenzhen synergy and major progress on AI governance and the Ukraine war. He highlighted the twin-city arrangement and Hong Kong's role in hosting delegates.
The upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen presents a prime opportunity to deepen cooperation between Hong Kong and its northern neighbor, while offering a platform for potential historic breakthroughs on artificial intelligence oversight and the conflict in Ukraine, according to Lan Kwai Fong Group chairman Allan Zeman.
Speaking in an interview, the veteran business leader noted that the twin-city arrangement, following the earlier APEC Finance Ministers' Meeting in Hong Kong, provides a significant advantage for the territory. He anticipated that numerous international business executives heading to the Shenzhen summit would choose to travel through or spend time in Hong Kong. Zeman also revealed that Hong Kong will stage the APEC Next-Gen Young Entrepreneurs Summit 2026 on 20 November, where he will appear as a keynote speaker. He added that the Lan Kwai Fong entertainment district is preparing to welcome delegates for evening dining and social gatherings throughout the event.
Zeman described Hong Kong and Shenzhen as sibling cities whose combined strengths can effectively propel mainland enterprises onto the global stage and accelerate the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area into a world-class economic zone. He highlighted Shenzhen's technological dynamism and artificial intelligence capabilities, noting that numerous high-quality mainland firms in the city are actively seeking international expansion. In turn, Hong Kong offers an established, globally trusted bridge anchored by its common law legal system, unrestricted capital flows, and international financial markets.
Reflecting on Shenzhen’s rapid modernization, Zeman remarked that global perspectives have shifted eastward, observing that parts of the Western world now face deteriorating conditions that contrast sharply with Asia's progress.
Having attended seven previous APEC conferences, Zeman emphasized that in-person diplomacy among top leaders remains indispensable amid volatile geopolitical tensions. While acknowledging that previous summits often concluded with general discussions rather than binding resolutions, he suggested that the upcoming gathering could deliver meaningful advancements on two major international issues involving the leaders of China, the United States, and Russia. The first potential breakthrough involves artificial intelligence. With worldwide apprehension growing over the unchecked development and existential risks posed by advanced automated systems, Zeman anticipated that the major powers might hold consultations aimed at establishing global safety guardrails and governance standards comparable to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons.
The second area of potential progress centers on the protracted Russia-Ukraine war. Zeman noted that tripartite discussions among the heads of state could explore pathways toward a ceasefire to halt casualties and ease the broader humanitarian crisis, an outcome that he said would deliver tremendous benefits to global stability.
Zeman framed the forthcoming bilateral and multilateral exchanges against an evolving political backdrop in Washington following the United States midterm elections, where the Republican Party lost its majority in Congress. He observed that United States President Donald Trump is likely to encounter substantial legislative hurdles domestically, creating a notable contrast with China's political continuity, the international stature of its leadership, and the sustained economic rise of Asia.

香港代表团访问卢森堡和德国深化与欧洲家族办公室的联系 |中国劳工公告栏
星期二, 17 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港代表团访问卢森堡和德国深化与欧洲家族办公室的联系
投资推广署于2026年11月14日至16日率团访问卢森堡和德国，推广香港作为家族办公室中心的地位。与欧洲投资者的会议探讨了跨境机会、企业继承和慈善事业。官员们表示，此行加强了香港作为全球金融中心的地位。
负责外国直接投资的政府机构投资推广署率领香港代表团于2026年11月14日至16日访问卢森堡和德国，以加深欧洲家族资本与亚洲市场之间的联系。代表团访问了卢森堡、法兰克福和慕尼黑，与家族办公室、家族企业、投资者和金融服务代表会面。
会议期间，港方分享了香港家族办公室生态系统的最新发展，并强调了香港作为全球最大跨境财富管理中心和亚洲顶级国际金融中心的优势。讨论内容涵盖跨境机遇、家族企业发展和继任规划等，旨在促进欧洲和亚洲市场之间的交流与合作。
投资推广署董事冯国强表示，香港拥有完善的家族办公室生态系统、稳定的投资环境和多元化的机会，是寻求长期增长、稳定和确定性的家族的理想基地。冯先生表示：“我们欢迎欧洲家庭在香港设立和拓展业务，并利用香港连接中国内地、亚洲和国际市场的平台，拓展其全球足迹和未来发展空间。”
代表团成员、海洋资本创始合伙人周运成表示，此次访问使欧洲家族和家族企业对香港蓬勃发展的家族办公室生态系统有了更深入的了解。 “我们就前沿投资策略、慈善事业、代际传承等核心话题进行了富有成效的对话，成功激发了欧洲家庭对香港市场的浓厚兴趣，”周说。
周小川补充说，香港在金融科技、另类投资、人工智能等新兴领域拥有领先优势。他表示：“加上政府持续的亲商政策和大量顶尖专业人才，香港可以为不同发展阶段的家庭提供全面的支持，为长期发展创造稳定和可持续的环境。”
是次访问进一步促进了香港与欧洲家族办公室、家族企业和金融界的交流，加深了欧洲市场对香港家族办公室生态系统和营商环境的了解。政府表示，此行凸显香港作为全球家族办公室中心的地位，并支持香港第一个五年经济社会发展规划（2026-2030年）和《2026年施政报告》，旨在巩固香港作为国际资产和财富管理中心的地位。
